title.en: Volume 321 Biographies 80: Zheng Xie, Chen Xiang, Qian Gongfu, Sun Zhu, Feng Ji, Lu Hui, Liu Shu, Liu Qi, Qian Yi, Zheng Xia
title.raw: 卷三百二十一 列傳第八十 鄭獬 陳襄 錢公輔 孫洙 豐稷 呂誨 劉述 劉琦 錢顗 鄭俠 Volume 321 Biographies 80: Zheng Xie, Chen Xiang, Qian Gongfu, Sun Zhu, Feng Ji, Lu Hui, Liu Shu, Liu Qi, Qian Yi, Zheng Xia

sentences.zh: 鄭獬，字毅夫，安州安陸人。

translations.literal: Zheng Xie, styled Yifu, was a native of Anlu in Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xie, whose courtesy name was Yifu, came from Anlu in Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 少負俊材，詞章豪偉峭整，流輩莫敢望。

translations.literal: In youth he possessed outstanding talent; his compositions were grand, powerful, steep, and orderly, and none of his contemporaries dared match him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he showed exceptional ability, and his writing was bold, imposing, and finely wrought—none among his peers dared measure himself against him.

sentences.zh: 進士第一。

translations.literal: He ranked first among jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: He took first place in the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 通判陳州，入直集賢院、度支判官、修起居注、知制誥。

translations.literal: He served as vice-prefect of Chenzhou, entered the Hanlin Academy as a duty scholar, became fiscal affairs judicial commissioner, compiled the Veritable Records, and was appointed draft edict compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice-prefect of Chenzhou, then served in the Academy of Scholarly Worthies, as fiscal affairs judicial commissioner, compiler of the Veritable Records, and draft edict compiler.

sentences.zh: 英宗郎位，治永昭山陵，悉用乾興制度，獬言：「今國用空乏，近者賞軍，已見橫斂，富室嗟怨，流聞京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, work began on the Yongzhao Imperial Tomb and the regulations of the Qianxing era were adopted in full. Xie said: "At present state revenues are depleted. Recently, in rewarding the army, we have already seen extortionate levies; wealthy households sigh with resentment, and word of this spreads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, construction of the Yongzhao Imperial Tomb proceeded under the full regulations of the Qianxing reign. Xie said: "State funds are now exhausted. The recent rewards to the army have already brought on heavy exactions; wealthy families groan in resentment, and reports of this reach the capital.

sentences.zh: 先帝節儉愛民，蓋出天性，凡服用器玩，極於樸陋，此天下所共知也。

translations.literal: The late emperor was frugal and loved the people—this sprang from his inborn nature. In all dress, utensils, and playthings he went to the utmost in plainness and austerity; this is known to all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor was thrifty and cared for the people by nature; in clothing, vessels, and ornaments he chose the plainest and simplest—this all the realm knows.

sentences.zh: 而山陵制度，乃欲效乾興最盛之時，獨不傷儉德乎？

translations.literal: Yet for the tomb regulations you wish to emulate the most lavish period of Qianxing—will this alone not wound his virtue of thrift?
translations.idiomatic: Yet the tomb is to follow the most extravagant standards of Qianxing—does that not alone tarnish his reputation for frugality?

sentences.zh: 願飭有司，損其名數。」

translations.literal: I beg that you instruct the responsible offices to reduce the names and numbers [of ritual items]."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the responsible offices be ordered to cut back the prescribed items and quantities."

sentences.zh: 又言：「天子初即位，郡國馳表稱賀，例官其人，此出五代餘習，因仍未改。

translations.literal: He also said: "When the Son of Heaven first ascends the throne, the commanderies and principalities dispatch memorials of congratulation and, by precedent, appoint those who present them to office. This comes from a leftover custom of the Five Dynasties and has continued unreformed.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When a new emperor takes the throne, the provinces rush in congratulatory memorials and, by custom, those who present them receive office. This is a remnant of Five Dynasties practice that has never been abolished.

sentences.zh: 今庶官猥眾，充溢銓曹。

translations.literal: Today common offices are numerous beyond reason and overflow the Bureau of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Common offices are now far too numerous and crowd the Bureau of Appointments.

sentences.zh: 況前日群臣進官，已布維新之澤，不須復行此恩，以開僥幸。」

translations.literal: Moreover, only the other day the court advanced the ranks of its ministers and has already spread the grace of renewal—there is no need to grant this favor again and open the door to opportunism."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the court has only just promoted the ministers and spread the grace of a new reign—there is no need to grant this favor again and encourage opportunism."

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None of these [memorials] received a response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these proposals received a reply.

sentences.zh: 又上疏言：「陛下初臨御，恭默不言，所與共政者七八大臣而已，焉能盡天下之聰明哉？

translations.literal: He again submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty has newly assumed the throne and keeps silent in respectful reserve; those who share in government are only seven or eight great ministers—how can you exhaust all the intelligence under Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial: "Your Majesty has just begun to rule and remains respectfully silent; only seven or eight great ministers share in government—how can you draw on all the wisdom under Heaven?

sentences.zh: 願申詔中外，許令盡言，有可采錄，召與之對。

translations.literal: I hope you will extend an edict within and without the court allowing everyone to speak freely; where there is something worth adopting, summon the speaker for a personal audience.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an edict go forth throughout the court and the provinces permitting frank speech, and that where something is worth adopting, the speaker be summoned for audience.

sentences.zh: 至於臣下進見，訪以得失，虛心求之，必能有益治道。」

translations.literal: As for your ministers coming forward to audience, inquire of them regarding successes and failures; seek humbly and you will surely benefit the art of governance."
translations.idiomatic: When your ministers come before you, question them on what succeeds and what fails; seek their counsel in humility, and governance will surely gain."

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor commended and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised and accepted this advice.

sentences.zh: 時詔諸郡敦遣遺逸之士，至則試之秘閣，命以官，頗有謬舉者，眾論喧嘩，旋即廢罷，獬言：「古之薦士，以謂拔十得五，猶得其半；

translations.literal: At the time an edict directed all commanderies earnestly to send forward reclusive scholars; upon arrival they were tested at the Secret Pavilion and given office. There were quite a few mistaken nominations, public discussion grew clamorous, and the measure was soon abolished. Xie said: "In antiquity when recommending scholars, it was said that if one selected ten and obtained five, one still had half;
translations.idiomatic: An edict then directed the commanderies to send up reclusive scholars; on arrival they were examined at the Secret Pavilion and given office. There were many mistaken nominations, public outcry grew loud, and the measure was soon dropped. Xie said: "In antiquity it was said that in recommending scholars, if ten were chosen and five proved worthy, one still had half;

sentences.zh: 況今所失未至十五，而遽以浮言廢之，可乎？

translations.literal: How much more so when today's losses do not reach one in fifteen—and you hasten to abolish the policy on empty talk—can this be right?
translations.idiomatic: how much more when today's failures do not reach one in fifteen—yet you hasten to abolish the policy on loose talk—is that right?

sentences.zh: 願復此科，使豪俊無遺滯之歎。」

translations.literal: I hope this examination will be restored, so that outstanding men feel no regret at being overlooked."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that this examination be restored, so that outstanding men need not lament being passed over."

sentences.zh: 未及行，出知荊南。

translations.literal: Before the measure could be implemented, he was sent out as prefect of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Before this could be carried out, he was sent out as prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 治平中，大水求言，獬上疏曰：「陛下側身思咎，念有以消復之，不知求忠言者，將欲用之邪？

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era, after great floods an edict sought advice. Xie submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty bends his person to reflect on fault and thinks how to dispel and remedy it—I do not know whether in seeking loyal words you intend truly to employ them,
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhiping era, after severe floods an edict called for counsel. Xie submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty bends himself to reflect on guilt and seeks means to dispel and remedy it—I do not know whether in seeking loyal counsel you mean truly to use it,

sentences.zh: 抑但舉故事邪？

translations.literal: or merely to enact precedent?
translations.idiomatic: or only to follow precedent?

sentences.zh: 觀前世之君，因變異以求諫者甚眾，及考其實，則能用其言而載於行事者，蓋亦鮮矣。

translations.literal: Considering emperors of previous ages, many sought remonstrance because of anomalies; yet when one examines the facts, those who could employ the advice and record it in their deeds were very few indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Looking at emperors of former ages, many sought remonstrance because of portents; yet when one examines the record, those who truly used such words and embodied them in action were very few.

sentences.zh: 今詔發天下忠義之士，必有極其所韞，以薦諸朝，一日萬機，勢未能盡覽，不過如平時下之中書、密院，至於無所行而後止。

translations.literal: Now the edict summons loyal and righteous men from all the realm; there will surely be those who give the utmost of what they harbor and recommend it to court. With ten thousand affairs in a day, Your Majesty cannot possibly read all; most likely it will be no more than routing them to the Secretariat and Privy Council as in normal times, until nothing can be enacted and they are dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Now the edict summons loyal and righteous men from across the realm; some will surely give the fullest of what they hold and offer it to court. With ten thousand affairs in a day, Your Majesty cannot read all; most likely they will be routed to the Secretariat and Privy Council as in ordinary times, until nothing can be done and they are set aside.

sentences.zh: 如是則與前世之為空言者等爾。

translations.literal: In that case it is no better than the empty words of previous ages.
translations.idiomatic: In that case it will be no different from the empty words of former ages.

sentences.zh: 謂宜選官置屬，掌所上章，與兩府近臣從容講貫，可則行之，否則罷之，有疑焉，則廣詢而決之。

translations.literal: I propose selecting officials and assigning assistants to take charge of submitted memorials, and together with close ministers of the two administrations to discuss them at leisure—where feasible, carry them out; where not, set them aside; where there is doubt, consult widely and decide.
translations.idiomatic: I propose that officials be chosen and staff assigned to receive submitted memorials, and that they discuss them at leisure with close ministers of the two administrations—where feasible, act; where not, set aside; where in doubt, consult widely and decide.

sentences.zh: 群臣得而眾事舉，此應天之實也。

translations.literal: When ministers gain a hearing and all affairs are advanced, this is the substance of responding to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When ministers are heard and affairs are carried through, this is the true way to respond to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 天下之進言也甚難，而上之受言也常忽。

translations.literal: For all under Heaven to offer counsel is very difficult, while those above frequently receive counsel with neglect.
translations.idiomatic: It is very hard for those below to offer counsel, and those above often receive it with neglect.

sentences.zh: 願陛下采群臣之章疏，容而聽之，史冊大書，以為某年大水，詔求直言，用某人之辭而求某事，以出夫前世之為空言者，無令徒掛牆壁為虛文而已。」

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will gather your ministers' memorials, grant them a hearing, and have the historians record in large characters that in such-and-such a year, after great floods an edict sought frank speech, and such-and-such a person's words were employed to seek such-and-such a matter—thus surpassing the empty speech of former ages, and not letting them merely hang on the wall as dead documents."
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will gather the memorials of your ministers, grant them a hearing, and have the historians record in full that in such-and-such a year, after great floods, an edict sought frank speech and such-and-such a man's words were used to accomplish such-and-such a matter—thus surpassing the empty speech of former ages, and not letting them hang on the wall as dead documents alone."

sentences.zh: 還，判三班院。

translations.literal: On returning [to the capital], he was made director of the Three-Ban Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: On his return to the capital, he was made director of the Three-Ban Bureau.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，召獬夕對內東門，命草吳奎知青州及張方平、趙抃參政事三制，賜雙燭送歸舍人院，外廷無知者。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Shenzong's reign, Xie was summoned for an evening audience inside the Inner Eastern Gate and ordered to draft three edicts appointing Wu Kui to know Qingzhou and Zhang Fangping and Zhao Bian as participating administrators of affairs. He was given paired candles to escort him back to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; the outer court knew nothing of this.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Shenzong's reign, Xie was summoned for an evening audience at the Inner Eastern Gate and ordered to draft three edicts—appointing Wu Kui to Qingzhou and Zhang Fangping and Zhao Bian as participating administrators of affairs. He was given paired candles to light his way back to the Academy of Scholarly Worthies; the outer court knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 遂拜翰林學士。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 朝廷議納橫山，獬曰：「兵禍必起於此。」

translations.literal: The court debated accepting the submission of Hengshan; Xie said, "War calamity will surely arise from this."
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated accepting the submission of Hengshan, Xie said, "Military disaster will surely begin here."

sentences.zh: 已而种諤取綏州，獬言：「臣竊見手詔，深戒邊臣無得生事。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Chong E took Suizhou; Xie said, "Your servant has seen the emperor's own hand-edict deeply warning border officials not to cause trouble on their own initiative.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Chong E seized Suizhou. Xie said, "I have seen the emperor's own hand-edict sternly warning border officials not to provoke trouble on their own.

sentences.zh: 今乃特尊用變詐之士，務為掩襲，如戰國暴君之所尚，豈帝王大略哉！

translations.literal: Now you specially honor and employ men of changing deceit who strive for surprise attacks, as the tyrants of the Warring States admired—how is this the broad strategy of an emperor?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now you specially honor men of shifting deceit who strive for surprise attacks, as the tyrants of the Warring States admired—how is this the broad strategy of an emperor?

sentences.zh: 諤擅興，當誅。」

translations.literal: E acted on his own authority and should be put to death."
translations.idiomatic: E acted on his own authority and should be executed."

sentences.zh: 又請因諒祚告哀，遣使立其嗣子，識者韙之。

translations.literal: He also requested that, because Liangzuo was reporting mourning, an envoy be sent to install his heir; men of insight praised this.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that, when Liangzuo reported mourning, an envoy be sent to install his heir—men of judgment approved.

sentences.zh: 權發遣開封府。

translations.literal: [He was] acting chief intendant of Kaifeng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting chief intendant of Kaifeng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 民喻興與妻謀殺一婦人，獬不肯用按問新法，為王安石所惡，出為侍讀學士、知杭州。

translations.literal: A commoner, Yu Xing, conspired with his wife to murder a woman; Xie refused to apply the new interrogation-by-torture law and incurred the hostility of Wang Anshi; he was sent out as academician reader-in-waiting and prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner named Yu Xing conspired with his wife to murder a woman; Xie refused to apply the new interrogation-by-torture law and earned Wang Anshi's enmity; he was sent out as academician reader-in-waiting and prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞呂誨乞還之，不聽。

translations.literal: The censor-in-chief Lü Hui begged that he be returned [to the capital]; the request was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Lü Hui begged that he be recalled; the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙青州。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 方散青苗錢，獬言：「但見其害，不忍民無罪而陷憲網。」

translations.literal: When the Green Sprouts money was being distributed, Xie said, "I see only its harm and cannot bear that the people, guiltless, should fall into the penal net."
translations.idiomatic: When Green Sprouts money was being distributed, Xie said, "I see only its harm and cannot bear that innocent people should fall into the penal net."

sentences.zh: 引疾祈閑，提舉鴻慶宮，卒，年五十一。

translations.literal: He cited illness to seek leisure, was made promoter of Hongqing Palace, and died at fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He cited illness to seek a quiet post, was made promoter of Hongqing Palace, and died at fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 家貧子弱，其柩藁殯僧屋十餘年，滕甫為安州，乃克葬。

translations.literal: His family was poor and his sons young; his coffin lay in rough burial in a monk's hall for more than ten years until Teng Fu became prefect of Anzhou and only then could he be buried.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and his sons still young; his coffin lay in a rough burial in a monk's hall for more than ten years until Teng Fu became prefect of Anzhou and at last he could be buried.

sentences.zh: 陳襄，字述古，福州侯官人。

translations.literal: Chen Xiang, styled Shugu, was a native of Houguan in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Xiang, whose courtesy name was Shugu, came from Houguan in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少孤，能自立，出遊鄉校，與陳烈、周希孟、鄭穆為友。

translations.literal: Orphaned young, he was able to stand on his own; he went out to the district school and befriended Chen Lie, Zhou Ximeng, and Zheng Mu.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, he supported himself, attended the district school, and befriended Chen Lie, Zhou Ximeng, and Zheng Mu.

sentences.zh: 時學者沉溺於雕琢之文，所謂知天盡性之說，皆指為迂闊而莫之講，四人者始相與倡道於海濱，聞者皆笑以驚，守之不為變，卒從而化，謂之「四先生」。

translations.literal: Scholars at the time were sunk in ornate composition; what was called the doctrine of knowing Heaven and exhausting one's nature they all dismissed as impractical and would not discuss. The four of them first promoted the Way together on the seacoast; listeners all laughed in astonishment, but they held firm without change until people followed and were transformed, and they were called the "Four Masters."
translations.idiomatic: Scholars of the day were lost in ornate prose; teachings on knowing Heaven and fulfilling one's nature were dismissed as impractical and left untaught. The four first preached the Way together on the coast—listeners laughed in shock, but they held their course until others followed and were transformed, and they were called the "Four Masters."

sentences.zh: 襄舉進士，調浦城主簿，攝令事。

translations.literal: Xiang passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief recorder of Pucheng, where he also assumed the magistrate's duties.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief recorder of Pucheng, where he also handled the magistrate's duties.

sentences.zh: 縣多世族，以請託脅持為常，令不能制。

translations.literal: The county had many hereditary great clans who routinely used entreaty and pressure as coercion, and the magistrate could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: The county had many powerful clans who routinely used influence and pressure as weapons, and the magistrate could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 襄欲稍革其俗，每聽訟，必使數吏環立於前。

translations.literal: Xiang wished gradually to reform these customs; whenever he heard lawsuits he always had several clerks stand in a ring before him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang wished to reform these customs gradually; whenever he heard a case he had several clerks stand in a ring before him.

sentences.zh: 私謁者不得發，老奸束手。

translations.literal: Private visitors could not get a word out; old schemers were helpless.
translations.idiomatic: Private petitioners could not speak; veteran schemers were left helpless.

sentences.zh: 民有失物者，賊曹捕偷兒至，數輩相撐拄，襄語之曰：「某廟鐘能辨盜，犯者捫之輒有聲，餘則否。」

translations.literal: When a commoner lost something, the constable arrested a band of petty thieves; several men shoved one another [accusing each other]. Xiang said to them, "A certain temple bell can identify thieves—the guilty who touch it will at once sound; the rest will not."
translations.idiomatic: When a commoner reported a theft, the constable brought in several petty thieves who accused one another. Xiang told them, "A certain temple bell can identify thieves—whoever is guilty will make it ring when he touches it; the innocent will not."

sentences.zh: 乃遣吏先引以行，自率同列詣鐘所祭禱，陰塗以墨，而以帷蔽之。

translations.literal: He then had clerks lead them on ahead and himself led his colleagues to the bell to sacrifice and pray, secretly smearing it with ink and screening it with a curtain.
translations.idiomatic: He sent clerks to lead them ahead and himself led his colleagues to the bell to offer sacrifice and prayer, secretly smearing it with ink and covering it with a curtain.

sentences.zh: 命群盜往捫，少焉呼出，獨一人手無所汙，扣之，乃為盜者；

translations.literal: He ordered the band to go touch it; after a little while he called them out—only one man had unstained hands; when questioned, he proved to be the thief;
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the band to touch the bell; shortly he called them out—only one had clean hands; under questioning he proved to be the thief;

sentences.zh: 蓋畏鐘有聲，故不敢觸，遂服罪。

translations.literal: for he feared the bell would sound and therefore dared not touch it; he thereupon confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He had feared the bell would ring and dared not touch it, and thereupon confessed.

sentences.zh: 知河陽縣，始教民種稻。

translations.literal: As prefect of Heyang County he first taught the people to plant rice.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Heyang County he first taught the people to plant rice.

sentences.zh: 富弼為郡守，一見即禮遇之。

translations.literal: Fu Bi, as prefect of the commandery, honored and treated him at first sight.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Bi, as prefect of the commandery, honored him at first meeting.

sentences.zh: 襄留意教化，進縣子弟於學。

translations.literal: Xiang devoted himself to moral instruction and advanced the county's young men into the school.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang devoted himself to moral education and enrolled the county's young men in the school.

sentences.zh: 或讒之於弼，謂其誘邑子以資過客，弼疑焉。

translations.literal: Someone slandered him to Bi, saying he was luring the township sons to provide for passing guests; Bi became suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Someone slandered him to Bi, saying he was using local youths to entertain traveling guests; Bi grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 人勸毀學舍以塞謗，不聽。

translations.literal: People urged him to destroy the school building to stop the slander; he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Others urged him to tear down the school to silence slander; he refused.

sentences.zh: 久之，弼以語襄，襄曰：「自反而縮，雖千萬人往矣。

translations.literal: After some time Bi spoke of this to Xiang; Xiang said, "If after examining myself I find no fault, though a thousand or ten thousand men come against me, what harm? [quoting Mencius]
translations.idiomatic: After some time Bi spoke of this to Xiang; Xiang said, "If after examining myself I am blameless, though thousands come against me, what harm?

sentences.zh: 公苟有惑志，何名知己。」

translations.literal: If you harbor doubts in your heart, how can you be called one who knows me?"
translations.idiomatic: If you harbor doubts, how can you be called one who knows me?"

sentences.zh: 益講說不少懈。

translations.literal: He lectured all the more without slackening.
translations.idiomatic: He lectured all the more without slackening.

sentences.zh: 弼由是愈益奇之，及入相，薦為秘閣校理、判祠部。

translations.literal: Bi came to admire him still more; when Bi entered the government as chief minister, he recommended Xiang as collator of the Secret Pavilion and judicial commissioner of the Sacrificial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Bi admired him still more; when Bi became chief minister he recommended Xiang as collator of the Secret Pavilion and judicial commissioner of the Sacrificial Bureau.

sentences.zh: 譯經僧死，遺表度十僧，列子廟三年度一道士，皆抑不行。

translations.literal: When a monk who was translating scriptures died, his memorial petition sought to ordain ten monks, and Liezi Temple sought every three years to ordain one Daoist—all were suppressed and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: When a scripture-translating monk died, his memorial asked to ordain ten monks, and Liezi Temple sought to ordain one Daoist every three years—all were denied.

sentences.zh: 知常州，運渠橫遏震澤，積水不得北入江，為常、蘇二州病。

translations.literal: As prefect of Changzhou, transport canals blocked Lake Zhen (Taihu) so that accumulated water could not flow north into the river, to the harm of Chang and Su prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Changzhou, transport canals dammed Lake Tai so that pooled water could not flow north into the river, harming Chang and Su prefectures.

sentences.zh: 襄度渠之丈尺與民田步畝，定其數，授以浚法。

translations.literal: Xiang measured the canal's dimensions against the people's field paces and acres, fixed the quotas, and gave them the method of dredging.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang measured the canal against the people's fields, fixed quotas, and taught them how to dredge.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遂削望亭古堰，水不復積。

translations.literal: Before long he cut down the ancient dyke at Wangting, and the water no longer pooled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he removed the ancient dyke at Wangting, and the water no longer backed up.

sentences.zh: 入為開封府推官、鹽鐵判官。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture and salt and iron judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture and salt and iron judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，奉使契丹，以設席小異於常，不即坐，契丹移檄疆吏，坐出知明州。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, [Xiang] was sent as envoy to the Khitan; because the seating arrangement differed slightly from usual, he would not immediately be seated; the Khitan shifted blame to the border officials, and he was demoted to know Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, Xiang was sent as envoy to the Khitan; because the seating differed slightly from custom he would not sit at once; the Khitan blamed the border officials, and he was demoted to prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，同修起居注，知諫院，改侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: The next year he was made co-compiler of the Veritable Records, knew the Remonstrance Bureau, and was changed to supervising censor with concurrent duties.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made co-compiler of the Veritable Records, head of the Remonstrance Bureau, and supervising censor with concurrent duties.

sentences.zh: 論青苗法不便，曰：「臣觀制置司所議，莫非引經以為言，而其實則稱貸以取利，事體卑削，貽中外譏笑。

translations.literal: He discussed the inconveniences of the Green Sprouts law, saying, "Your servant observes that what the Fiscal Affairs Commission proposes invariably cites the classics as its language, while in substance it is lending at interest to take profit—the matter is mean and impoverished and invites ridicule within and without.
translations.idiomatic: He criticized the Green Sprouts law, saying, "What the Fiscal Affairs Commission proposes always cites the classics, yet in substance it is lending at interest for profit—the matter is base and invites ridicule at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 是特管夷吾、商鞅之術，非聖世所宜行。

translations.literal: This is nothing but the art of Guan Zhong and Lord Shang—not what a sage age should practice.
translations.idiomatic: This is the art of Guan Zhong and Lord Shang—not what a sage age should practice.

sentences.zh: 望貶斥王安石、呂惠卿以謝天下。」

translations.literal: He hoped Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing would be demoted to console all under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: He asked that Wang Anshi and Lü Huiqing be demoted to console the realm."

sentences.zh: 又乞罷韓絳政府，以杜大臣爭利而進者，且言韓維不當為中丞，劉述、范純仁等無罪，宜復官。

translations.literal: He also begged to dismiss Han Jiang from the government to shut off ministers who advance through contention over profit, and said Han Wei should not be censor-in-chief; Liu Shu, Fan Chunren, and others were guiltless and should be restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to remove Han Jiang from government to block ministers who advance through profit-seeking, said Han Wei should not be censor-in-chief, and that Liu Shu, Fan Chunren, and others were innocent and should be restored.

sentences.zh: 皆不聽，而召試知制誥。

translations.literal: None of this was heard; instead he was summoned for examination for draft edict compiler.
translations.idiomatic: None of this was heeded; instead he was summoned to examination for draft edict compiler.

sentences.zh: 襄以言不行，辭不肯試，願補外。

translations.literal: Because his words had no effect, Xiang declined and refused to take the examination, asking to fill an outside post.
translations.idiomatic: Because his counsel had no effect, Xiang declined the examination and asked for an outside post.

sentences.zh: 安石欲以為陝西轉運使，帝惜其去，留修起居注。

translations.literal: Anshi wished to make him Shaanxi transport commissioner; the Emperor regretted losing him and kept him to compile the Veritable Records.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi wished to make him Shaanxi transport commissioner; the Emperor regretted losing him and kept him to compile the Veritable Records.

sentences.zh: 襄懇辭，手詔諭之，乃就職。

translations.literal: Xiang earnestly declined; the Emperor personally wrote an edict to instruct him, and only then did he accept the post.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang earnestly declined; the Emperor wrote a personal edict instructing him, and only then did he accept.

sentences.zh: 逾年，為知制誥，安石又欲出之，帝不許。

translations.literal: After a year he became draft edict compiler; Anshi again wished to send him out, but the Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he became draft edict compiler; Anshi again wished to send him out, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 尋直學士院，安石益忌之，擿其書詔小失，出知陳州，徙杭州，以樞密直學士知通進銀臺司兼侍讀，判尚書都省。

translations.literal: Before long he was made academy academician; Anshi hated him all the more, picked at a small error in his edict, and sent him out to know Chenzhou, then transferred to Hangzhou, then as Privy Council academician knew the Court of Imperial Entertainments and was attendant reader, with concurrent duty over the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made academy academician; Anshi hated him more, seized on a small error in his edict, and sent him to Chenzhou, then Hangzhou, then as Privy Council academician he headed the Court of Imperial Entertainments and served as attendant reader with concurrent duty over the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十四，贈給事中。

translations.literal: He died at sixty-four; posthumously he was made Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-four and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 襄蒞官所至，必務興學校。

translations.literal: Wherever Xiang held office he invariably devoted himself to establishing schools.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Xiang held office he devoted himself to establishing schools.

sentences.zh: 平居存心以講求民間利病為急。

translations.literal: In daily life he applied his mind chiefly to investigating the hardships and benefits of the common people.
translations.idiomatic: In daily life he chiefly studied the hardships and benefits of the common people.

sentences.zh: 既亡，友人劉尋視其篋，得手書累數十幅，盈紙細書，大抵皆民事也。

translations.literal: After his death his friend Liu looked through his chest and found several dozen sheets written by his own hand, the paper covered with fine script—mostly all were matters of the people's welfare.
translations.idiomatic: After his death his friend Liu searched his chest and found dozens of sheets in his own hand, covered with fine script—nearly all concerned the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 在經筵時，神宗顧之甚厚，嘗訪人材之可用者。

translations.literal: When he was on the Classics Mat, Shenzong regarded him very highly and once inquired about talented men who might be employed.
translations.idiomatic: When he served on the Classics Mat, Shenzong regarded him highly and once asked which talented men might be employed.

sentences.zh: 襄以司馬光、韓維、呂公著、蘇頌、范純仁、蘇軾至於鄭俠三十三人對，謂光、維、公著皆股肱心膂之臣，不當久外；

translations.literal: Xiang offered thirty-three names from Sima Guang, Han Wei, Lü Gongzhu, Su Song, Fan Chunren, and Su Shi down to Zheng Xia, saying Guang, Wei, and Gongzhu were all ministers at the heart of the throne and should not long remain outside;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang named thirty-three men from Sima Guang, Han Wei, Lü Gongzhu, Su Song, Fan Chunren, and Su Shi down to Zheng Xia, saying Guang, Wei, and Gongzhu were heart-and-soul ministers who should not long remain outside court;

sentences.zh: 謂俠愚直敢言，發於忠義，投竄瘴癘，朝不謀夕，願使得生還。

translations.literal: as for Xia, he said he was simple, upright, and dared to speak, motivated by loyalty and righteousness, cast into malarial wastes with the court not planning past the morrow—he hoped Xia might be allowed to return alive.
translations.idiomatic: as for Xia, he was simple, upright, and outspoken from loyalty, cast into the southern wastes with the court not planning past tomorrow—he hoped Xia might be allowed to return alive.

sentences.zh: 帝不能盡用。

translations.literal: The Emperor could not employ them all.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor could not employ them all.

sentences.zh: 錢公輔

translations.literal: Qian Gongfu
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gongfu

sentences.zh: 錢公輔，字君倚，常州武進人。

translations.literal: Qian Gongfu, styled Junyi, was a native of Wujin in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Gongfu, whose courtesy name was Junyi, came from Wujin in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 少從胡翼之學，有名吳中。

translations.literal: In youth he studied under Hu Yizhi and was famous in Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied under Hu Yizhi and was renowned in the Wu region.

sentences.zh: 第進士甲科。

translations.literal: He placed in the top grade of the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the top grade of the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 通判越州，為集賢校理、同判吏部南曹。

translations.literal: He was vice-prefect of Yuezhou, collator of the Imperial Archives, and concurrent judicial commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice-prefect of Yuezhou, collator of the Imperial Archives, and concurrent judicial commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 歷開封府推官、戶部判官、知明州。

translations.literal: He served successively as investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture, Ministry of Revenue judicial commissioner, and prefect of Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as investigating officer of Kaifeng Prefecture, Ministry of Revenue judicial commissioner, and prefect of Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 衙前法以三等差次勞勤，應格者聽指酒場以自補，富者足欲而貧得日困，充募益鮮；

translations.literal: The yamen-runner law graded labor by three ranks of toil; those who met the standard were permitted to assign themselves wine-fields for self-support—the rich had enough and the poor grew daily poorer, and willing enlistees grew ever fewer;
translations.idiomatic: The yamen-runner law graded labor in three ranks; those who qualified could assign themselves wine-fields for support—the rich had enough while the poor grew poorer, and willing runners grew scarce;

sentences.zh: 額有不足，至役鄉民，破產不供費。

translations.literal: when quotas fell short they even conscripted villagers, who went bankrupt and could not supply the expense.
translations.idiomatic: when quotas fell short they conscripted villagers, who went bankrupt and could not meet the cost.

sentences.zh: 公輔取酒場官鬻之，分輕重以給役者，不復調民。

translations.literal: Gongfu took over the wine-fields as government sale and allocated light and heavy [duties] to supply the runners, no longer levying on the people.
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu made the wine-fields government-operated and allocated duties by weight to supply the runners, no longer levying on the people.

sentences.zh: 同修起居注，進知制誥。

translations.literal: He was co-compiler of the Veritable Records and advanced to draft edict compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He was co-compiler of the Veritable Records and advanced to draft edict compiler.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，陳《治平十議》，大要言采民政，分吏課，擇守宰，置二府官屬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong ascended the throne, Gongfu submitted the Ten Discourses on Orderly Rule; in broad outline they spoke of gathering popular complaints for governance, dividing official evaluations, selecting prefects and magistrates, and appointing staff for the Two Departments.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong came to the throne, Gongfu submitted the Ten Discourses on Orderly Rule, chiefly urging that popular grievances be gathered for governance, official evaluations be separated, prefects and magistrates be chosen carefully, and staff be appointed for the Two Departments.

sentences.zh: 又作《帝問》一篇上之。

translations.literal: He also wrote an essay entitled "The Emperor's Inquiry" and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote an essay entitled The Emperor's Inquiry and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 王疇為翰林學士未久，擢副樞密，公輔謂疇素望淺，不草制。

translations.literal: Wang Chou had been Hanlin academician only briefly when he was promoted to vice military affairs commissioner; Gongfu said Chou's standing had always been shallow and refused to draft the appointment edict.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chou had been a Hanlin academician only briefly when he was promoted to vice military affairs commissioner. Gongfu held that Chou's reputation was too thin and refused to draft the appointment edict.

sentences.zh: 帝以初政用大臣，而公輔格詔，謫為滁州團練使，議者以為重，呂誨等上章救之，不得。

translations.literal: The emperor, in early administration, was employing great ministers, yet Gongfu resisted the edict and was demoted to military training commissioner of Chuzhou; commentators thought the punishment heavy; Lu Hui and others submitted memorials to save him, without success.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was appointing senior ministers at the start of his reign, but Gongfu defied the order and was demoted to military training commissioner of Chuzhou. Commentators thought the punishment severe. Lu Hui and others memorialized in his defense, but to no avail.

sentences.zh: 逾年，起知廣德軍。

translations.literal: After a year he was recalled to serve as prefect of the Guangde Army.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was recalled to serve as prefect of the Guangde Army.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，拜天章閣待制、知鄧州，復知制誥。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Hanlin attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns and prefect of Dengzhou, then again draft edict compiler.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was appointed Hanlin attendant of the Hall of Heavenly Patterns and prefect of Dengzhou, then again draft edict compiler.

sentences.zh: 入見，帝勞苦之，使錄《十議》以進，命知諫院。

translations.literal: Upon entering audience, the emperor expressed sympathy for his hardships, had him record the Ten Discourses to submit, and appointed him head of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When he came before the throne, the emperor commiserated with his labors, ordered him to copy out the Ten Discourses for submission, and made him head of the Remonstrance Bureau.

sentences.zh: 嘗至中書白事，富弼謂曰：「上求治如饑渴，正賴君輩同心以濟。」

translations.literal: Once when he came to the Central Secretariat to report business, Fu Bi said to him: "The emperor seeks good governance as one thirsting and hungering—we rely on you gentlemen to work in unison to accomplish it."
translations.idiomatic: Once when he came to the Central Secretariat on business, Fu Bi told him, "The emperor thirsts for good government; we are counting on men like you to pull together and make it happen."

sentences.zh: 公輔曰：「朝廷所為是，天下誰敢不同！

translations.literal: Gongfu said: "When the court does what is right, who under Heaven would dare disagree!
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu replied, "When the court is right, who in the realm would dare dissent!

sentences.zh: 所為非，公輔欲同之，不可得已。」

translations.literal: When what is done is wrong, even if Gongfu wished to agree, it would be impossible."
translations.idiomatic: When it is wrong, even if I wanted to go along, I could not."

sentences.zh: 王安石雅與之善，既得志，排異己者，出滕甫鄆州，公輔數於帝前言甫不當去。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi had long been on good terms with him, but once he achieved his aims and purged those who disagreed, expelling Teng Fu to Yunzhou, Gongfu repeatedly told the emperor that Fu should not have been removed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi had always been close to him, but once Anshi got his way and drove out dissenters—sending Teng Fu to Yunzhou—Gongfu repeatedly told the emperor that Fu ought not to have been dismissed.

sentences.zh: 薛向更鹽法，安石主其議，而公輔謂向當黜，遂拂安石意，罷諫職，旋出知江寧府。

translations.literal: Xue Xiang revised the salt law, and Anshi supported his proposal, but Gongfu said Xiang should be dismissed; this went against Anshi's wishes, he was stripped of his remonstrance post, and soon after was sent out as prefect of Jiangning.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Xiang overhauled the salt law, Anshi backed him, but Gongfu argued that Xue should be removed. That defied Anshi's wishes; Gongfu lost his remonstrance post and was soon sent out as prefect of Jiangning.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝欲召還，安石言其助小人為異議，不宜在左右，但徙揚州。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor wished to recall him, but Anshi said he aided petty men in raising dissent and should not be near the throne—he was merely transferred to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor wanted him back, but Anshi said he helped petty men stir up opposition and should not stay at court; he was only moved to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以病乞越，改提舉崇福觀，卒，年五十二。

translations.literal: On grounds of illness he requested exemption and was changed to superintendent of the Chongfu Abbey; he died at age fifty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness and asked to be excused, was reassigned as superintendent of the Chongfu Abbey, and died at fifty-two.

sentences.zh: 孫洙，字臣源，廣陵人。

translations.literal: Sun Zhu, styled Chenyuan, was a native of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zhu, courtesy name Chenyuan, was from Guangling.

sentences.zh: 羈丱能文，未冠擢進士。

translations.literal: From childhood he could write; before coming of age he was selected as jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he could write; before he came of age he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 包拯、歐陽修、吳奎舉應制科，進策五十篇，指陳政體，明白剴切。

translations.literal: Bao Zheng, Ouyang Xiu, and Wu Kui recommended him for the imperial examination category; he submitted fifty policy essays pointing out the state of government, clear and incisive.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Zheng, Ouyang Xiu, and Wu Kui recommended him for the special imperial examination; he submitted fifty policy essays on the body politic, lucid and cutting.

sentences.zh: 韓琦讀之，太息曰：「慟哭流涕，極論天下事，今之賈誼也。」

translations.literal: Han Qi read them and sighed deeply: "Wailing and weeping, exhaustively discussing affairs of the realm—he is a Jia Yi of today."
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi read them and sighed, "Weeping and wailing, he exhaustively discusses the affairs of the realm—today's Jia Yi."

sentences.zh: 再遷集賢校理、知太常禮院。

translations.literal: He was transferred again to collator of the Imperial Archives and head of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to collator of the Imperial Archives and director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 治平中求言，以洙應詔疏時弊要務十七事，後多施行，兼史館檢討、同知諫院，乞增諫員以廣言路。

translations.literal: During the Zhiping era when the throne sought counsel, Zhu responded to the edict with a memorial on seventeen urgent contemporary abuses, many later implemented; concurrently archive collator and associate head of the Remonstrance Bureau; he asked to increase remonstrance staff to broaden the avenue of counsel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhiping era, when the throne called for counsel, Zhu answered with a memorial on seventeen pressing abuses of the day, many of which were later adopted. He also served as archive collator and associate head of the Remonstrance Bureau, and asked that remonstrance posts be increased to widen the path of criticism.

sentences.zh: 凡有章奏，輒焚其稿，雖親子弟不得聞。

translations.literal: Whenever he submitted memorials he burned the drafts—even close kin and sons were not allowed to know.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he drafted a memorial he burned the manuscript; not even his own sons were allowed to see it.

sentences.zh: 王安石主新法，多逐諫官御史，洙知不可，而鬱鬱不能有所言，但力求補外，得知海州。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi led the new laws and drove out many remonstrance officials and censors; Zhu knew resistance was futile yet was depressed and could not speak out, only striving to obtain an outer post, becoming prefect of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi pushed the new laws and purged many remonstrance officials and censors. Zhu knew protest was useless, yet brooded in silence and could say nothing; he only pressed for an outside appointment and became prefect of Haizhou.

sentences.zh: 免役法行，常平使者欲加斂緡錢，以取贏為功，洙力爭之。

translations.literal: When the exemption-from-corvée law was implemented, the Ever-Normal Granary emissary wished to levy additional cash to take surplus as merit; Zhu vigorously contested it.
translations.idiomatic: When the exemption-from-corvée law took effect, the Ever-Normal Granary commissioner wanted to levy extra cash and treat surplus as achievement; Zhu fought it hard.

sentences.zh: 方春旱，發運使調民浚漕渠以通鹽舸，洙持之不下，三上奏乞止其役。

translations.literal: In spring drought, the transport commissioner conscripted people to dredge canals for salt boats; Zhu withheld approval, thrice memorializing to halt the labor.
translations.idiomatic: During a spring drought the transport commissioner drafted people to dredge the canal for salt barges. Zhu held the order back and three times memorialized to stop the work.

sentences.zh: 旱蝗為害，致禱於朐山，撤奠，大雨，蝗赴海死。

translations.literal: During drought and locust plague, he prayed at Mount Xiong; after removing the offerings, great rain fell and locusts died in the sea.
translations.idiomatic: When drought and locusts ravaged the land, he prayed on Mount Xiong. After the offerings were withdrawn, heavy rain fell and the locusts died in the sea.

sentences.zh: 尋幹當三班院。

translations.literal: Soon after he took charge of the Three-Class Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon put in charge of the Three-Class Bureau.

sentences.zh: 三班員過萬數，功罪籍不明，前後牴牾，吏左右出入，公為欺奸。

translations.literal: The bureau had more than ten thousand members, but records of merit and fault were unclear, contradicted one another before and after, and clerks controlled access and exit, openly practicing fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Its membership exceeded ten thousand, yet merit and fault records were a muddle, old and new entries conflicted, and clerks controlled every in and out, openly cheating the office.

sentences.zh: 洙革其甚者八事，定為令。

translations.literal: Zhu reformed the eight worst abuses and fixed them as regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu corrected the eight worst abuses and codified them as law.

sentences.zh: 同修起居注，進知制誥。

translations.literal: He was co-compiler of the Veritable Records and promoted to draft edict compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He served as co-compiler of the Veritable Records and was promoted to draft edict compiler.

sentences.zh: 先是，百官遷敘，用一定之詞，洙建言：「群臣進秩，事理各異，而同用一詞；

translations.literal: Previously, when officials were promoted in rank, a single fixed formula was used. Zhu submitted a proposal: "When ministers advance in rank, the circumstances differ in each case, yet the same wording is used for all;
translations.idiomatic: Before this, promotions of officials all used one fixed formula. Zhu proposed, "When ministers rise in rank, the circumstances differ, yet one phrase serves for all;

sentences.zh: 至或一門之內，數人拜恩，名體散殊，而格以一律。

translations.literal: sometimes even within one household several people receive grace on the same day—the titles and forms are scattered and distinct, yet all are forced into one pattern.
translations.idiomatic: sometimes even within one family several people receive honors at once, their titles and forms all different, yet all are squeezed into the same mold.

sentences.zh: 苟從簡便，非所以暢王言、重命令也。」

translations.literal: If one follows convenience alone, that is not the way to give full expression to the king's words and to lend weight to commands."
translations.idiomatic: To take the easy way is not how to give full voice to the sovereign's words or lend dignity to his commands."

sentences.zh: 詔自今封贈蔭補，每大禮一易，他皆隨等撰定。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that henceforth, for enfeoffment, patronage appointment, and supplementary rank at each grand ceremony the wording would be revised once, and in other cases drafted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: An edict followed: henceforth, for enfeoffment, patronage appointment, and supplementary rank, each grand ceremony would bring one revision of the wording; other cases would be drafted according to rank.

sentences.zh: 元豐初，兼直學士院。

translations.literal: In the early Yuanyou era he concurrently served in the Hanlin Academy Direct Office.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Yuanyou era he also served in the Hanlin Academy Direct Office.

sentences.zh: 澶州河平，作靈津廟，詔洙為之碑，神宗獎其文。

translations.literal: When the Yellow River stabilized at Chanyang, the Lingjin Temple was built; an edict had Zhu compose its stele, and Shenzong praised his writing.
translations.idiomatic: When the river at Chanyang was brought to peace, the Lingjin Temple was built. Zhu was ordered to write its stele inscription, and Shenzong praised the text.

sentences.zh: 擢翰林學士，才逾月，得疾。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Hanlin academician, but barely a month later fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Hanlin academician, but fell ill barely a month later.

sentences.zh: 時參知政事闕，帝將用之，數遣中使、尚醫勞問。

translations.literal: The vice grand councilor post was vacant, and the emperor intended to appoint him, repeatedly sending palace envoys and imperial physicians to inquire after his health.
translations.idiomatic: With the vice grand councilor post empty, the emperor meant to use him and repeatedly sent palace envoys and court physicians to ask after his health.

sentences.zh: 入朝期日，洙小愈，在家習肄拜跽，僨不能興，於是竟卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: On the day set for entering court, Zhu had slightly recovered and was at home practicing kneeling and prostration when he collapsed and could not rise; he died at age forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he was to enter court he had improved slightly and was at home practicing kneeling and bowing when he collapsed and could not get up. He died at forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 帝臨朝嗟惜，常賻外賜錢五十萬。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned at court; beyond the usual bereavement gift he granted fifty thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved at court and, beyond the usual funeral gift, gave fifty thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 洙博聞強識，明練典故，道古今事甚有條理。

translations.literal: Zhu was broadly learned with a strong memory, well versed in precedent, and discussed events ancient and modern with great order.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu was widely read and had a formidable memory. He knew precedent inside out and spoke of past and present with clear order.

sentences.zh: 出語皆成章，雖對親狎者，未嘗發一鄙語。

translations.literal: His speech always formed complete compositions—even with intimates he never uttered a vulgar word.
translations.idiomatic: Everything he said came out fully formed; even with close friends he never let slip a coarse word.

sentences.zh: 文詞典麗，有西漢之風。

translations.literal: His literary style was classical and elegant, with the flavor of Western Han.
translations.idiomatic: His writing was classical and fine, with the tone of Western Han.

sentences.zh: 士大夫共以丞輔期之，不幸早世，一時憫傷焉。

translations.literal: Officials jointly looked to him for grand councilor rank, but he died young, to the grief of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials alike expected him for the highest office, but he died young, and the age mourned him.

sentences.zh: 豐稷，字相之，明州鄞人。

translations.literal: Feng Ji, styled Xiangzhi, was a native of Yin in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji, courtesy name Xiangzhi, was from Yin in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 登第，為穀城令，以廉明稱。

translations.literal: After passing the examinations he served as magistrate of Gucheng, renowned for integrity and clarity.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the examinations he was magistrate of Gucheng, known for integrity and clear judgment.

sentences.zh: 從安燾使高麗，海中大風，檣折，舟幾覆，眾惶擾莫知所為，稷獨神色自若。

translations.literal: While accompanying An Yan on a mission to Goryeo, a great wind at sea snapped the mast and the boat nearly capsized; the crowd panicked while Ji alone remained composed.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Goryeo with An Yan, a gale at sea snapped the mast and the vessel nearly overturned. The company panicked, but Ji alone kept his composure.

sentences.zh: 燾歎曰：「豐君未易量也。」

translations.literal: Yan sighed: "Master Feng is not easily measured."
translations.idiomatic: Yan sighed, "Master Feng is not a man one can easily take the measure of."

sentences.zh: 知封丘縣，神宗召對，問：「卿昔在海中遭風波，何以不畏？」

translations.literal: As magistrate of Fengqiu, Shenzong summoned him for audience and asked: "When you once encountered wind and waves at sea, why were you unafraid?"
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Fengqiu he was summoned for audience. Shenzong asked, "When you met wind and waves at sea, why were you not afraid?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「巨浸連天，風濤固其常耳，憑仗威靈，尚何畏！」

translations.literal: He replied: "The vast ocean touches the sky—wind and waves are its constant state; relying on Your Majesty's august power, what is there to fear!"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "The great sea reaches to the sky; wind and waves are its ordinary way. With Your Majesty's majesty to rely on, what is there to fear!"

sentences.zh: 帝悅，擢監察御史。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and promoted him to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 治參知政事章惇請託事，無所移撓，出惇陳州。

translations.literal: He prosecuted Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Dun for solicitation and yielded to no pressure, resulting in Dun's exile to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He prosecuted Vice Grand Councilor Zhang Dun for using influence and would not bend; Dun was sent out to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 徒著作佐郎、吏部員外郎，提點利州、成都路刑獄。

translations.literal: He was transferred to assistant editorial director and vice minister of the Ministry of Personnel, then intendant of criminal justice for Lizhou and Chengdu circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to assistant editorial director and vice minister of Personnel, then intendant of criminal justice for Lizhou and the Chengdu circuit.

sentences.zh: 入為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He entered service as palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as palace censor.

sentences.zh: 上疏哲宗曰：「陛下明足以察萬事之統，而不可用其明；

translations.literal: He memorialized to Emperor Zhezong: "Your Majesty's clarity suffices to perceive the common thread of ten thousand affairs, yet clarity cannot be used;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to Emperor Zhezong: "Your Majesty is clear enough to grasp the thread running through ten thousand affairs, yet that clarity is not used;

sentences.zh: 智足以應變曲當，而不可用其智。

translations.literal: your wisdom suffices to respond aptly to every turn, yet wisdom cannot be used.
translations.idiomatic: your wisdom is enough to meet every change aptly, yet that wisdom is not used.

sentences.zh: 順考古道，二帝所以聖；

translations.literal: By reverently examining ancient ways, the Two Emperors became sage;
translations.idiomatic: By reverently studying the ancient Way, the Two Emperors became sage;

sentences.zh: 儀刑文王，成王所以賢。

translations.literal: by patterning oneself on King Wen, King Cheng became worthy.
translations.idiomatic: by taking King Wen as model, King Cheng became worthy.

sentences.zh: 願以《洪範》為元龜，祖訓為寶鑒，一動一言，思所以為則於四海，為法於千載，則教化行，習俗美，而中國安矣。」

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty take the Hong Fan as the great tortoise and ancestral instructions as the precious mirror—every act and word, considering how to be a model for the four seas and a law for a thousand generations, then teaching will prevail, customs will be fine, and China will be secure."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty take the Hong Fan as your great oracle and ancestral instruction as your bright mirror, so that every move and every word is weighed as a standard for the four seas and a model for a thousand years. Then teaching will spread, custom will be refined, and the realm will be secure."

sentences.zh: 劉奉世冊立夏國嗣子乾順，而乾順來賀坤成節，奉世遽出境，稷劾之，奉世以贖論，遷右司諫。

translations.literal: Liu Fengshi was tasked with installing the Xixia heir Qianshun, yet when Qianshun came to congratulate the Kuncheng festival, Fengshi hurriedly crossed the border; Ji impeached him and Fengshi was penalized by redemption fine, while Ji was promoted to supervising censor of the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fengshi had been sent to invest the Xixia heir Qianshun, yet when Qianshun came to congratulate the Kuncheng festival Fengshi abruptly left the border. Ji impeached him; Fengshi was punished by fine, and Ji was promoted to supervising censor of the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 揚、荊二王為天子叔父，尊寵莫並，密令蜀道織錦茵，稷於正衙論曰：「二聖以儉先天下，而宗王僭侈，官吏奉承，皆宜糾正。」

translations.literal: The Prince of Yang and Prince of Jing, the emperor's paternal uncles, enjoyed matchless honor; secretly they ordered Shu route brocade carpet-makers, and Ji argued at the main hall: "The two sage emperors took frugality as their lead for the realm, yet imperial princes are extravagant and officials fawn—all should be corrected."
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yang and Prince of Jing, the emperor's uncles, enjoyed unmatched favor; they secretly ordered brocade carpets woven on the Shu route. Ji argued in the main hall, "The two sage emperors led the realm in thrift, yet imperial princes grow lavish and officials flatter them—all this should be corrected."

sentences.zh: 既退，御史趙㞦謂曰：「聞君言，使幾汗流浹背。」

translations.literal: After retiring, Censor Zhao Fang said to him: "Hearing your words almost made me sweat through the back."
translations.idiomatic: After he withdrew, Censor Zhao Fang told him, "Hearing you speak nearly made the sweat run down my back."

sentences.zh: 改國子司業、起居舍人，歷太常少卿、國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was changed to vice director of the Directorate of Education, diarist, successively vice director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship, and director of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to vice director of the Directorate of Education and diarist, then successively vice director of the Court of Sacrificial Worship and director of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 車駕幸太學，命講《書·無逸篇》，賜四品服，除刑部侍郎兼侍講。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage visited the Imperial Academy, he was ordered to lecture on the "Against Luxurious Ease" chapter of the Documents; he was granted fourth-rank robes and appointed vice minister of Justice with concurrent lecturing duties.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited the Imperial Academy, Ji was ordered to lecture on the "Against Luxurious Ease" chapter of the Documents. He was granted fourth-rank robes and made vice minister of Justice with concurrent lecturing duties.

sentences.zh: 元祐八年春，多雪，稷言：「今嘉祥未臻，沴氣交作，豈應天之實未充，事天之禮未備，畏天之誠未孚歟？

translations.literal: In spring of the eighth year of Yuanyou, snow was frequent; Ji said: "Auspicious signs have not yet arrived and baleful forces interact—could it be that the substance of responding to Heaven is insufficient, the rites of serving Heaven are incomplete, or reverence toward Heaven is not sincere?
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the eighth year of Yuanyou snow fell often. Ji said, "Auspicious omens have not yet appeared and baleful forces are at work—is the substance of answering Heaven insufficient, the rites of serving Heaven incomplete, or reverence for Heaven not yet sincere?

sentences.zh: 宮掖之臣，有關預政事，如天聖之羅崇勳、江德明，治平之任守忠者歟？

translations.literal: Are there palace attendants interfering in government, like Luo Chongxun and Jiang Deming in the Tiansheng era, or Ren Shouzhong in the Zhiping era?
translations.idiomatic: Are there palace attendants meddling in government, as Luo Chongxun and Jiang Deming did in the Tiansheng era, or Ren Shouzhong in the Zhiping era?

sentences.zh: 願陛下昭聖德，祗天戒，總正萬事，以消災祥。」

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty display sage virtue, revere Heaven's warnings, and set right all affairs to dispel calamities."
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty show forth sage virtue, heed Heaven's warnings, and set all affairs straight to dispel these omens."

sentences.zh: 帝親政，召內侍居外者樂士宣等數人。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally took up government, he recalled several eunuchs who had been posted outside, including Le Shixuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally took the reins, he recalled several eunuchs who had been posted outside, among them Le Shixuan.

sentences.zh: 稷言：「陛下初親萬機，未聞登進忠良，而首召近幸，恐上累大德。」

translations.literal: Ji said: "Your Majesty has just taken up the myriad responsibilities; I have not yet heard of promoting the loyal and good, yet the first summons are to close favorites—I fear this will weigh upon your great virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "Your Majesty has only just begun to handle the myriad affairs of state. I have not yet heard of advancing the loyal and worthy, yet the first summons go to close favorites. I fear this will burden your great virtue."

sentences.zh: 以集賢院學士知潁州、江寧府，拜吏部侍郎，又出知河南府，加龍圖閣待制。

translations.literal: As academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies he governed Yingzhou and Jiangning, was appointed vice minister of Personnel, then sent out again as prefect of Henan, and was given the appointment as Hanlin attendant-in-waiting of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: As academician of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies he governed Yingzhou and Jiangning, was made vice minister of Personnel, then sent out again as prefect of Henan and given the post of Hanlin attendant-in-waiting of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 章惇欲困以道路，連歲亟徙六州。

translations.literal: Zhang Dun wished to wear him down on the road and moved him through six prefectures in consecutive years.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun meant to wear him down with travel and moved him through six prefectures in as many years.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，以左諫議大夫召，道除御史中丞，入對，與蔡京遇，京越班揖曰：「天子自外服召公中執法，今日必有高論。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Huizong ascended, Ji was summoned as left remonstrance grandee; en route he was appointed chief investigating censor; entering audience he encountered Cai Jing, who stepped out of rank and bowed: "His Majesty recalled you from outer service to wield the law at the center—today there must be weighty counsel."
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne, Ji was summoned as left remonstrance grandee and, on the road, appointed chief investigating censor. Entering audience he met Cai Jing, who stepped forward out of rank and bowed, "His Majesty recalled you from the provinces to enforce the law at court—today there must be weighty counsel."

sentences.zh: 稷正色答曰：「行自知之。」

translations.literal: Ji answered gravely: "You will know my conduct when you see it."
translations.idiomatic: Ji answered sternly, "You will know when you see it."

sentences.zh: 是日，論京奸狀，既而陳瓘、江公望皆言之，未能動。

translations.literal: That day he denounced Jing's misconduct; afterward Chen Guan and Jiang Gongwang also spoke, but could not shake Jing.
translations.idiomatic: That day he denounced Jing's wrongdoing. Later Chen Guan and Jiang Gongwang spoke as well, but could not move him.

sentences.zh: 稷語陳師錫等曰：「京在朝，吾屬何面目居此？」

translations.literal: Ji said to Chen Shixi and others: "With Jing in court, what face have we to remain here?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji told Chen Shixi and the others, "With Jing in court, what face do we have sitting here?"

sentences.zh: 擊之不已，京遂去翰林。

translations.literal: He pressed the attack without cease and Jing finally left the Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: He kept pressing the attack without letup, and Jing finally left the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 又乞辨宣仁誣謗之禍，且言：「史臣以王安石《日錄》亂《神宗實錄》，今方修《哲宗實錄》，願申飭之。」

translations.literal: He also petitioned to clarify the calumny against Empress Dowager Xuanren, saying: "Historians used Wang Anshi's Daily Records to corrupt the Veritable Records of Shenzong; now the Veritable Records of Zhezong is being compiled—I pray give strict orders.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked that the slander against Empress Dowager Xuanren be cleared, saying, "Historians used Wang Anshi's Daily Records to corrupt the Veritable Records of Shenzong. Now the Veritable Records of Zhezong is being compiled—I pray Your Majesty give strict orders."

sentences.zh: 時宦官漸盛，稷懷《唐書·仇士良傳》讀於帝前，讀數行，帝曰：「已諭。」

translations.literal: As eunuchs gradually grew powerful, Ji brought the Tang History biography of Qiu Shiliang and read it before the emperor; after several lines the emperor said: "I understand."
translations.idiomatic: As eunuchs gradually grew stronger, Ji brought the Tang History biography of Qiu Shiliang and read it before the emperor. After a few lines the emperor said, "I understand."

sentences.zh: 稷為若不聞者，讀畢乃止。

translations.literal: Ji acted as if he had not heard and continued until he finished reading.
translations.idiomatic: Ji behaved as if he had not heard and read on until he finished.

sentences.zh: 曾布得助嬖昵，將拜相，稷約其僚共論之。

translations.literal: Zeng Bu, aided by favorites, was about to be made chief councillor; Ji arranged with his colleagues jointly to condemn this.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Bu, backed by favorites, was about to become chief councillor. Ji arranged with his colleagues to denounce this together.

sentences.zh: 俄轉工部尚書兼侍讀，布遂相。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to minister of Works with concurrent lecturing duty, and Bu became chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was moved to minister of Works with concurrent lecturing duties, and Bu became chief councillor.

sentences.zh: 稷謝表有佞臣之語，帝問為誰，對曰：「曾布也。

translations.literal: Ji's thank-you memorial contained language about sycophants; the emperor asked who was meant; he replied: "Zeng Bu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's thank-you memorial spoke of sycophants. The emperor asked whom he meant. He answered, "Zeng Bu.

sentences.zh: 陛下斥之外郡，則天下事定矣。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty banishes him to an outer commandery, affairs under Heaven will be settled."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends him out to a distant prefecture, affairs under Heaven will be settled."

sentences.zh: 改禮部。

translations.literal: He was changed to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 論宋用臣不當賜美諡，不為書敕。

translations.literal: He argued that Song Yongchen should not be granted a fine posthumous title and refused to draft the edict.
translations.idiomatic: He argued that Song Yongchen should not receive a flattering posthumous title and refused to draft the edict.

sentences.zh: 哲宗升祔，議功臣配享，稷以為當用司馬光、呂公著。

translations.literal: When Zhezong was enshrined alongside the ancestors and meritorious ministers were debated for paired sacrifice, Ji held that Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu should be used.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong was enshrined and meritorious ministers were debated for paired sacrifice in the ancestral temple, Ji held that Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu should be chosen.

sentences.zh: 或謂二人嘗得罪，不可用。

translations.literal: Some said both had once offended and could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: Some said both had once given offense and could not be used.

sentences.zh: 稷曰：「止論其有功於時爾，如唐五王豈非得罪於中宗，何嫌於配享？」

translations.literal: Ji said: "One considers only their service to the age—as in Tang, were not the Five Princes offenders against Emperor Zhongzong, yet what objection to paired sacrifice?"
translations.idiomatic: Ji said, "One looks only at their service to the age. In Tang, did not the Five Princes offend Emperor Zhongzong—what bar is there to paired sacrifice?"

sentences.zh: 又言：「陛下以『建中靖國』紀元，臣謂尊賢納諫，舍己從人，是謂『建中』；

translations.literal: He also said: "Your Majesty takes Jianzhong Jingguo as the era name; I hold that revering the worthy and accepting remonstrance, abandoning the self to follow others—that is 'Jianzhong';
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Your Majesty has taken Jianzhong Jingguo as the era name. I hold that honoring the worthy and heeding remonstrance, setting aside the self to follow others—that is Jianzhong;

sentences.zh: 不作奇技淫巧，毋使近習招權，是謂『靖國』。

translations.literal: not making strange arts and excessive crafts, not allowing close attendants to grasp power—that is 'Jingguo'.
translations.idiomatic: not making odd contrivances and extravagant crafts, not letting close attendants seize power—that is Jingguo.

sentences.zh: 以副體元謹始之義。」

translations.literal: This is to fulfill the meaning of founding the era with reverent beginning."
translations.idiomatic: That would fulfill the meaning of opening an era with reverent care."

sentences.zh: 禁內織錦緣宮簾為地衣，稷言：「仁宗衾褥用黃絁，服御用縑繒，宜守家法。」

translations.literal: Within the palace, brocade along palace curtains was woven as floor covering; Ji said: "Emperor Renzong's bedding used yellow gauze and imperial dress used silk and cotton—Your Majesty should guard the household law."
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace, brocade from palace curtains was woven into floor coverings. Ji said, "Emperor Renzong's bedding used yellow gauze and imperial dress used plain silk and cotton. Your Majesty should keep to the household law."

sentences.zh: 詔罷之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the practice halted.

sentences.zh: 稷盡言守正，帝待之厚，將處之尚書左丞，而積忤貴近，不得留，竟以樞密直學士守越。

translations.literal: Ji spoke his mind in uprightness; the emperor treated him generously and was about to place him as left vice grand councilor, but repeated clashes with powerful favorites meant he could not remain and was finally made Hanlin attendant-in-waiting and prefect of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Ji spoke uprightly to the end. The emperor treated him generously and meant to make him left vice grand councilor, but because he repeatedly offended powerful favorites he could not stay and was finally made Hanlin attendant-in-waiting and prefect of Yue.

sentences.zh: 蔡京得政，修故怨，貶海州團練副使、道州別駕，安置台州。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing took power he settled old scores, demoting him to military training vice commissioner of Haizhou and prefectural administrator of Daozhou, settled at Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing took power he settled old scores, demoting Ji to military training vice commissioner of Haizhou and prefectural administrator of Daozhou, with residence assigned at Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 除名徙建州，稍復朝請郎。

translations.literal: His name was struck from the rolls and he was moved to Jianzhou, later restored slightly to court-greeting gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was struck from the rolls and exiled to Jianzhou, later restored in part to court-greeting gentleman.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 建炎中，追復學士，諡曰清敏。

translations.literal: During the Jianyan era his Hanlin rank was posthumously restored and he was given the posthumous title Qingmin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyan era his Hanlin rank was posthumously restored and he was given the posthumous title Qingmin.

sentences.zh: 初，文彥博嘗品稷為人似趙抃，及賜諡，皆以「清」得名。

translations.literal: Earlier Wen Yanbo had once appraised Ji as resembling Zhao Bian, and when the posthumous title was granted both were honored with "Qing" in the name.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wen Yanbo had judged Ji's character akin to Zhao Bian's, and when the posthumous title was granted both men were honored with "Qing" in the name.

sentences.zh: 稷三任言責，每草疏，必密室，子弟亦不得見。

translations.literal: Ji thrice bore remonstrance responsibility; whenever he drafted memorials he sealed himself in a private room—even sons and younger brothers could not see.
translations.idiomatic: Ji three times held remonstrance office. Whenever he drafted a memorial he shut himself in a private room—even sons and younger brothers were not allowed to see.

sentences.zh: 退多焚稿，未嘗以時政語人。

translations.literal: After retiring he burned most drafts and never spoke of current affairs to others.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he burned most drafts and never discussed current affairs with others.

sentences.zh: 所薦士如張庭堅、馬涓、陳瓘、陳師錫、鄒浩、蔡肇，皆知名當世雲。

translations.literal: Those he recommended—including Zhang Tingjian, Ma Juan, Chen Guan, Chen Shixi, Zou Hao, and Cai Zhao—were all renowned in their age.
translations.idiomatic: Men he recommended—Zhang Tingjian, Ma Juan, Chen Guan, Chen Shixi, Zou Hao, Cai Zhao—were all celebrated in their day.

sentences.zh: 論曰：熙寧行新法，輕進少年爭趨競進，老成知務者逡巡引退，何其見幾之明耶？

translations.literal: The commentary says: When the new laws were implemented in Xining, young men rushed forward in competition while seasoned men who understood affairs held back and withdrew—how clear their foresight!
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: In the Xining era, when the new laws were launched, young men scrambled to advance while seasoned men who knew better hung back and withdrew—how sharp their foresight!

sentences.zh: 獬議論剴切，精練民事，青苗法行，獬獨幡然求去，至窘迫不堪，弗恤也。

translations.literal: Xie spoke incisively and was skilled in civilian affairs; when the Green Sprouts law was implemented Xie alone resolutely sought to leave, even to distress beyond bearing, without care.
translations.idiomatic: Xie's discourse was cutting and he was skilled in the people's affairs. When the Green Sprouts law took effect, Xie alone turned away and sought to leave, even when pressed to the breaking point, without wavering.

sentences.zh: 襄奮起海隅，屢折不變，學者卒從而化，乃心民事，死猶不已。

translations.literal: Xiang rose from the seacoast, repeatedly struck down yet unchanged; scholars ultimately followed and were transformed; he devoted his heart to the people's affairs, and after death did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang rose from the seacoast, was struck down again and again yet never changed; scholars in the end followed and were transformed. He gave his heart to the people's affairs, and even in death did not stop.

sentences.zh: 公輔以忤安石見黜，洙為諫官不能言，至免役取贏，洙方力爭，所謂不揣其本者歟！

translations.literal: Gongfu was dismissed for opposing Anshi; Zhu as remonstrance official could not speak—only when the exemption law sought surplus did he strive to oppose—is this not failing to grasp the root?
translations.idiomatic: Gongfu was dismissed for crossing Anshi; Zhu, though a remonstrance official, could not speak—only when the exemption law sought surplus did he fight back. Is this not failing to strike at the root?

sentences.zh: 稷劾蔡京，論司馬光、呂公著當配享廟庭，蓋亦名侍從也。

translations.literal: Ji impeached Cai Jing and argued Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu should be paired in the temple hall—he too was a famed attendant-in-waiting.
translations.idiomatic: Ji impeached Cai Jing and argued that Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu should share sacrifice in the temple hall—he too was a famed attendant-in-waiting.

sentences.zh: 呂誨，字獻可，開封人。

translations.literal: Lü Hui, styled Xianké, was a native of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Hui, whose courtesy name was Xianké, came from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 祖端，相太宗、真宗。

translations.literal: His grandfather Duan served as chief minister under Emperors Taizong and Zhenzong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Duan had served as chief minister under Emperors Taizong and Zhenzong.

sentences.zh: 誨性純厚，家居力學，不妄與人交。

translations.literal: Hui's character was pure and generous; at home he studied diligently and did not casually associate with people.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Hui was honest and steadfast; he devoted himself to study at home and kept company only with care.

sentences.zh: 進士登第，由屯田員外郎為殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and rose from Vice Director of the Directorate of Tuntian to Attendant Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination, he rose from vice director of the Directorate of Tuntian to palace attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣多上章訐人罪，誨言：「臺諫官許風聞言事，蓋欲廣采納以補闕政。

translations.literal: At the time many court officials submitted memorials impeaching others' crimes. Hui said, "Censorial and remonstrance officials are permitted to speak on the basis of hearsay in order to broaden collection and adoption [of reports] and remedy government shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: At the time many officials were submitting memorials accusing their colleagues of crimes. Hui said, "Censorial and remonstrance officials are allowed to report matters on hearsay precisely so the throne may gather more counsel and remedy shortcomings in governance.

sentences.zh: 苟非職分，是為侵官。

translations.literal: If it is outside one's official duty, it constitutes encroachment on another's office.
translations.idiomatic: When it falls outside one's proper duties, that is encroachment on another office.

sentences.zh: 今乃詆斥平生，暴揚曖昧，刻薄之態浸以成風，請下詔懲革。」

translations.literal: Now they slander and condemn others' entire lives and expose ambiguous matters; a harsh and ungenerous attitude has gradually become the prevailing custom. I ask that an edict be issued to punish and reform this."
translations.idiomatic: Today officials vilify men's whole lives and parade ambiguous affairs into the open; such harshness has gradually become the prevailing habit. I ask that an edict be issued to punish and reform it."

sentences.zh: 樞密副使程戡結貴幸，致位政地，誨疏其過，以宣徽使判延州。

translations.literal: Deputy Commissioner of Military Affairs Cheng Kan curried favor with the powerful and attained a position in the governing center. Hui submitted a memorial on his faults, and [Cheng was appointed] Military Affairs Commissioner administering Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The deputy commissioner of military affairs Cheng Kan had curried favor with the powerful to reach the seat of government. Hui memorialized his faults, and Cheng was reassigned as military affairs commissioner administering Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 復上言：「戡以非才罷，不宜更委邊任；

translations.literal: He submitted again: "Since Kan was removed for lack of talent, he should not again be entrusted with frontier duty;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted again: "Since Kan was dismissed for lack of talent, he ought not be entrusted again with frontier duties;
