sentences.zh: 宣徽使地高位重，非戡所當得也。」

translations.literal: the post of Military Affairs Commissioner is lofty in rank and weighty in position—not one Cheng ought to receive."
translations.idiomatic: the post of military affairs commissioner is high in rank and grave in responsibility—not one Cheng deserved."

sentences.zh: 兗國公主薄其夫，夜開禁門入訴。

translations.literal: The Princess of Yanguo slighted her husband, and at night opened the forbidden gate to enter and plead her case.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Yanguo treated her husband with contempt and, at night, had the forbidden gate opened to enter the palace and plead her case.

sentences.zh: 誨請並劾閽吏，且治主第宦者罪，悉逐之。

translations.literal: Hui asked that the gate officials be impeached together [with her], and that the eunuchs of the princess's residence also be punished—all were expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked that the gatekeepers be impeached as well, and that the eunuchs of the princess's residence be punished; all were expelled.

sentences.zh: 御藥供奉官四人遙領團練使，御前忠佐當汰復留，誨劾樞密使宋庠陰求援助，徇私紊法。

translations.literal: Four Imperial Pharmacy supply officials remotely held regimental commissioner titles; Palace Loyal Assistants who ought to have been culled were kept instead. Hui impeached Military Affairs Commissioner Song Qi for secretly seeking support, showing partiality and disrupting the law.
translations.idiomatic: Four imperial pharmacy supply officials held regimental commissioner titles in absentia; palace loyal assistants who ought to have been culled were retained instead. Hui impeached military affairs commissioner Song Qi for secretly soliciting support, showing favoritism and disturbing the law.

sentences.zh: 詔罷庠而用陳升之為副使，誨又論之。

translations.literal: An edict dismissed Qi and appointed Chen Shengzhi deputy commissioner; Hui again argued against this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict removed Qi and made Chen Shengzhi deputy commissioner; Hui argued against the appointment again.

sentences.zh: 升之既去，誨亦出知江州，時嘉祐六年也。

translations.literal: Once Shengzhi had departed, Hui also went out as prefect of Jiangzhou—it was the sixth year of Jiayou.
translations.idiomatic: After Shengzhi left office, Hui was also sent out as prefect of Jiangzhou, in the sixth year of the Jiayou era.

sentences.zh: 上疏請蚤建皇嗣，曰：「竊聞中外臣僚，以聖嗣未立，屢有密疏請擇宗人。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial asking that an imperial heir be established early, saying, "I have heard that court and provincial officials, because the sacred heir has not been established, have repeatedly submitted secret memorials asking that a clansman be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial urging that an imperial heir be established without delay, saying, "I hear that officials inside and outside the court, because no imperial heir has yet been named, have repeatedly submitted secret memorials asking that a member of the imperial clan be chosen.

sentences.zh: 唯陛下思忠言，奮獨斷，以遏未然之亂。

translations.literal: I only hope Your Majesty will consider loyal words, exert independent judgment, and check disorder before it arises.
translations.idiomatic: I only ask that Your Majesty heed loyal counsel, act with resolute independent judgment, and check disorder before it arises.

sentences.zh: 又聞太史奏，彗躔心宿，請備西北。

translations.literal: I have also heard the grand astrologer report that a comet crossed the Heart constellation and ask that the northwest be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: I have also heard the grand astrologer report that a comet had crossed the Heart constellation and ask that defenses in the northwest be strengthened.

sentences.zh: 按《天文志》，心為天王正位，前星為太子，直則失勢，明則見祥。

translations.literal: According to the "Treatise on Astronomy," the Heart is the proper seat of the Heavenly King; the front star is the Crown Prince—if upright it means loss of power; if bright, auspicious signs appear.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Treatise on Astronomy, the Heart is the proper seat of the Heavenly King and the front star represents the crown prince—when upright it signifies loss of power; when bright it signals good omen.

sentences.zh: 今既直且暗，而妖彗乘之，臣恐咎證不獨在西北也。

translations.literal: Now it is both upright and dim, and an ominous comet rides upon it—I fear the signs of blame lie not only in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Now it stands upright yet dim, with an ominous comet upon it—I fear the portents of blame reach beyond the northwest alone.

sentences.zh: 自夏及秋，雨淫地震，陰盛之沴，固有冥符。

translations.literal: From summer through autumn there have been excessive rains and earthquakes—the calamities of yin in excess surely have their portents in the unseen realm.
translations.idiomatic: From summer through autumn there have been excessive rains and earthquakes; calamities born of yin in excess surely carry their signs in the unseen world.

sentences.zh: 近者宗室之中，訛言事露，流傳四方，人心駭惑，窺覦之志，可不防其漸哉！

translations.literal: Recently within the imperial clan rumors have been exposed and spread in all directions; hearts are alarmed and confused, and designs of covetous observation—can one fail to guard against them at their first stirrings!
translations.idiomatic: Recently within the imperial clan scandalous rumors have come to light and spread in every direction; people are alarmed and unsettled, and covetous designs are stirring—surely these must be checked at the first sign!

sentences.zh: 願為社稷宗廟計，審擇親賢，稽合天意，宸謀已定，當使天下共知。

translations.literal: I wish for the sake of the altars of state and the ancestral temple that a worthy kinsman be carefully chosen, that it accord with Heaven's intent, and that once the imperial deliberation is settled, all under Heaven should know together.
translations.idiomatic: For the sake of the altars of state and the ancestral temple, I ask that a worthy kinsman be chosen with care, that the choice accord with Heaven's intent, and that once Your Majesty's decision is firm it be made known to all under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 萬一有奸臣附會其間，陽為忠實，以緩上心，此為患最大，不可不察也。」

translations.literal: If by any chance crafty ministers attach themselves to the matter, outwardly loyal and sincere while easing the sovereign's mind—this would be the greatest harm and cannot fail to be examined."
translations.idiomatic: If by any chance crafty ministers should attach themselves to the affair, posing as loyal and sincere while lulling Your Majesty's resolve—that would be the gravest danger and must not go unexamined."

sentences.zh: 仁宗以誨章付中書韓琦，由此定議。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong handed Hui's memorial to the chief minister Han Qi, and by this the decision was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong handed Hui's memorial to Chief Minister Han Qi, and the decision was settled accordingly.

sentences.zh: 召為侍御史，改同知諫院。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Attendant Censor and changed to Associate Director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as attendant censor and made associate director of the remonstrance bureau.

sentences.zh: 英宗不豫，誨請皇太后日命大臣一員，與淮陽王視進藥餌。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong was unwell, Hui asked that the Empress Dowager daily appoint one chief minister to join the Prince of Huaiyang in overseeing the administration of medicine.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yingzong fell ill, Hui asked that the empress dowager daily appoint one senior minister to join the Prince of Huaiyang in supervising the administration of medicine.

sentences.zh: 都知任守忠用事久，帝之立非守忠意，數間諜東朝，播為惡言，內外洶懼。

translations.literal: Palace Intendant Ren Shouzhong had long held power; the emperor's installation had not been according to Shouzhong's intent, and he repeatedly sent spies to the eastern palace spreading malicious words—inside and outside were in turmoil and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Palace intendant Ren Shouzhong had long held power; the emperor's accession had not been Shouzhong's wish, and he repeatedly sent spies to the eastern palace spreading slander—in and out of court were in turmoil and fear.

sentences.zh: 誨上兩宮書，開陳大義，詞旨深切，多人所難言者。

translations.literal: Hui submitted letters to the Two Palaces, setting forth the great principles in language deep and earnest—much that many found hard to speak.
translations.idiomatic: Hui submitted letters to both palaces setting forth the fundamental principles in language deep and earnest—much that others found difficult to say.

sentences.zh: 帝疾小愈，屢言乞親萬幾。

translations.literal: The emperor's illness improved somewhat, and he repeatedly asked to attend personally to the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor's illness eased somewhat, he repeatedly asked to resume personal governance.

sentences.zh: 太后歸政，誨言於帝曰：「后輔佐先帝歷年，閱天下事多矣。

translations.literal: When the Empress Dowager returned the government, Hui said to the emperor, "The Empress Dowager assisted the late emperor for many years and has seen much of affairs under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When the empress dowager returned power to the throne, Hui said to the emperor, "The empress dowager assisted the late emperor for many years and has seen far more of the realm's affairs than you.

sentences.zh: 事之大者，宜關白諮訪然後行，示弗敢專。」

translations.literal: On great matters, you should inform and consult her before acting, showing that you dare not decide alone."
translations.idiomatic: On great matters you ought to inform and consult her before acting, showing that you dare not decide alone."

sentences.zh: 遂論守忠平生罪惡，並其黨史昭錫竄之南方。

translations.literal: He then argued Shouzhong's lifelong crimes, and together with his faction-member Shi Zhaoxi had them banished to the south.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized against Shouzhong's lifelong crimes and, together with his ally Shi Zhaoxi, had them banished to the south.

sentences.zh: 內臣王昭明等為陝西四路鈐轄，專主蕃部。

translations.literal: Inner officials Wang Zhaoming and others served as Frontier Commissioners of the four routes of Shaanxi, exclusively managing tribal departments.
translations.idiomatic: The inner officials Wang Zhaoming and others served as frontier commissioners on the four Shaanxi routes, charged exclusively with tribal affairs.

sentences.zh: 誨言：「自唐以來，舉兵不利，未有不自監軍者。

translations.literal: Hui said, "Since the Tang, whenever the raising of troops has gone badly, there has never been a case not originating from military supervisors.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Since Tang times, whenever military campaigns have gone badly, the trouble has never failed to begin with military supervisors.

sentences.zh: 今走馬承受官品至卑，一路已不勝其害，況鈐轄乎？」

translations.literal: Now the circuit bearers of urgent dispatches are of the lowest official rank—one route already cannot bear their harm; how much less frontier commissioners?"
translations.idiomatic: Today the dispatch-bearers on horseback are of the lowest rank—one circuit already cannot endure the harm they do; how much less frontier commissioners?"

sentences.zh: 卒罷之。

translations.literal: In the end [the posts] were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the end the posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 治平二年，遷兵部員外郎，兼侍御史知雜事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiping he was promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War and concurrently Attendant Censor with charge of miscellaneous matters.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhiping he was promoted to vice director of the ministry of war and concurrently made chief attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 上言：「臺諫者，人主之耳目，期補益聰明，以防壅蔽。

translations.literal: He submitted: "The censorate and remonstrance officials are the sovereign's eyes and ears, expected to supplement and improve his clarity and guard against obstruction and concealment.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial: "The censorate and remonstrance officials serve as the sovereign's eyes and ears, meant to sharpen his judgment and guard against obstruction and concealment.

sentences.zh: 舊三院御史，常有二十員，而後益衰減，蓋執政者不欲主上聞中外之闕失。

translations.literal: Formerly the three bureaus of censors regularly had twenty officers, but afterward they were ever more reduced—for the chief ministers did not wish the sovereign to hear of shortcomings inside and outside [the court].
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the three censorial bureaus regularly had twenty officers, but their number had steadily dwindled, for those in power did not wish the sovereign to hear of shortcomings within and beyond the court.

sentences.zh: 今臺闕中丞，御史五員，惟三人在職，封章十上，報聞者八九。

translations.literal: Now the censorate lacks its vice-director; of five censor posts only three are filled and in service. Ten sealed memorials submitted—eight or nine receive acknowledgment.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate now lacked its vice-director; of five censor posts only three were actually serving. Of ten sealed memorials submitted, eight or nine received mere acknowledgment.

sentences.zh: 諫官二人，一他遷，一出使，言路壅塞，未有如今日之甚者。

translations.literal: Of two remonstrance officers, one transferred elsewhere, one sent on embassy—the avenues of speech were blocked as never before in severity as today.
translations.idiomatic: Of the two remonstrance officers, one had transferred elsewhere and one had been sent on diplomatic missions—the channels of remonstrance were blocked as never in memory.

sentences.zh: 竊為陛下羞之。」

translations.literal: I privately feel shame for Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: I am privately ashamed for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，即命邵必知諫院。

translations.literal: The emperor read the memorial and immediately appointed Shao Bi director of the remonstrance bureau.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read the memorial and immediately appointed Shao Bi director of the remonstrance bureau.

sentences.zh: 於是濮議起，侍從請稱王為皇伯，中書不以為然，誨引義固爭。

translations.literal: Then the Pu-title controversy arose; the attendant officials asked that the prince be styled Imperial Uncle, the Secretariat disagreed, and Hui cited principle and argued steadfastly.
translations.idiomatic: Then arose the controversy over titles for Prince Pu; the attendant officials proposed calling the prince Imperial Uncle, the secretariat disagreed, and Hui cited principle and argued stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 會秋大水，誨言：「陛下有過舉而災沴遽作，惟濮王一事失中，此簡宗廟之罰也。」

translations.literal: When autumn brought great floods, Hui said, "Your Majesty has made improper acts and disasters have suddenly appeared; only on the matter of Prince Pu have you missed the mark—this is punishment for slighting the ancestral temple."
translations.idiomatic: When great autumn floods struck, Hui said, "Your Majesty's missteps have brought calamity swiftly upon us; only in the matter of Prince Pu have you missed the mark—this is punishment for slighting the ancestral temple."

sentences.zh: 郊廟禮畢，復申前議，七上章，不聽；

translations.literal: When the suburban and temple rites were complete, he again pressed his earlier view; seven memorials submitted, not heeded;
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban and temple rites were complete, he pressed his earlier argument again; he submitted seven memorials without being heeded;

sentences.zh: 乞解臺職，亦不聽。

translations.literal: he asked to be released from censorial duties, and this too was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to be relieved of his censorial post, and this too was denied.

sentences.zh: 遂劾宰相韓琦不忠五罪，曰：「昭陵之土未乾，遽欲追崇濮王，使陛下厚所生而薄所繼，隆小宗而絕大宗。

translations.literal: He then impeached Chief Minister Han Qi on five charges of disloyalty, saying, "The soil of Zhaoling is not yet dry, yet you hasten to posthumously honor Prince Pu, causing Your Majesty to favor the biological and slight the adopted, exalt the minor line and extinguish the major line.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached Chief Minister Han Qi on five counts of disloyalty, saying, "The earth over Zhaoling is not yet dry, yet you hasten to posthumously honor Prince Pu, causing Your Majesty to favor your biological father and slight your adopted one—to exalt the lesser line and extinguish the greater.

sentences.zh: 言者論辨累月，琦猶遂非，不為改正，中外憤鬱，萬口一詞。

translations.literal: Remonstrators argued for months, yet Qi still persisted in error and would not correct it—inside and outside were aggrieved and distressed, ten thousand mouths with one voice.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrators debated for months, yet Qi still clung to his error and refused to correct it—throughout the realm people were aggrieved, and all spoke with one voice.

sentences.zh: 願黜居外藩，以慰士論。」

translations.literal: I wish that he be demoted to reside in an outer fief to comfort the judgment of the scholar-officials."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that he be demoted to a post in the outer provinces to satisfy public opinion among the scholar-officials."

sentences.zh: 又與御史范純仁、呂大防共劾歐陽修「首開邪議，以枉道說人主，以近利負先帝，陷陛下於過舉。」

translations.literal: Together with Censors Fan Chunren and Lü Dafang he jointly impeached Ouyang Xiu, [saying he] "first opened heterodox opinion, used crooked doctrine to persuade the sovereign, used immediate advantage to betray the late emperor, and trapped Your Majesty in improper acts."
translations.idiomatic: Together with censors Fan Chunren and Lü Dafang he jointly impeached Ouyang Xiu for "having first opened heterodox opinion, using perverse doctrine to persuade the sovereign, trading immediate advantage against the late emperor's intent, and trapping Your Majesty in a wrongful course."

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: All went unanswered.
translations.idiomatic: None received response.

sentences.zh: 已而詔濮王稱親，誨等知言不用，即上還告敕，居家待罪，且言與輔臣勢難兩立。

translations.literal: Before long an edict styled Prince Pu as kin; Hui and others knowing their words were not used, immediately submitted return of their patents of appointment, stayed home awaiting punishment, and said they could hardly coexist with the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict styled Prince Pu as kin; knowing their remonstrance had failed, Hui and the others returned their commissions, remained at home awaiting punishment, and declared that they could not coexist with the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 帝以問執政，修曰：「御史以為理難並立，若臣等有罪，當留御史。」

translations.literal: The emperor asked the chief ministers; Xiu said, "The censors believe coexistence is logically impossible—if we are guilty, the censors should remain."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted the chief ministers; Ouyang Xiu said, "The censors hold that coexistence is impossible—if we ministers are in the wrong, the censors ought to remain."

sentences.zh: 帝猶豫久之，命出御史，既而曰：「不宜責之太重。」

translations.literal: The emperor hesitated for a long time and ordered the censors sent out, then said, "They should not be punished too severely."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor hesitated at length, then ordered the censors dismissed; afterward he said, "They ought not be punished too harshly."

sentences.zh: 乃下遷誨工部員外郎、知蘄州。

translations.literal: Hui was demoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and made prefect of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was demoted to vice director of the ministry of works and appointed prefect of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，徙晉州，加集賢殿修撰、知河中府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, [Hui] was transferred to Jinzhou, given the additional title Academic Editor of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and made prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shenzong acceded, Hui was transferred to Jinzhou, made academic editor of the Hall for Gathering Worthies, and appointed prefect of Hezhong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 召為鹽鐵副使，擢天章閣待制，復知諫院，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Vice Commissioner of the Salt and Iron Commission, promoted to Hanlin Academician in Waiting, again made director of the remonstrance bureau, and appointed censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice commissioner of the salt and iron commission, promoted to academician in waiting at the Hall of Heavenly Manifestation, restored as director of the remonstrance bureau, and appointed censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 初，中旨下京東買金數萬兩，又令廣東市真珠，傳云將備宮中十閣用度。

translations.literal: At first secret imperial orders went out to buy tens of thousands of taels of gold in Jingdong and to purchase pearls in Guangdong—rumor said it was to supply the expenses of the ten pavilions within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first secret imperial orders went out to buy tens of thousands of taels of gold in Jingdong and pearls in Guangdong; rumor had it the purchases were to supply the ten palace pavilions.

sentences.zh: 誨言：「陛下春秋富盛，然聰明睿知，以天下為心，必不留神於此，願亟罷之。」

translations.literal: Hui said, "Your Majesty's years are full and vigorous, and your intelligence is keen and wise; with all under Heaven as your heart, you surely will not fix attention on this. I wish it be quickly stopped."
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Your Majesty is in the prime of life, keen and wise, with the realm at heart—you surely cannot mean to fix your attention on such things. I ask that the orders be revoked at once."

sentences.zh: 王安石執政，時多謂得人。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi held the government, many at the time said the right man had been found.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi took power, many said the throne had found the right man.

sentences.zh: 誨言其不通時事，大用之，則非所宜。

translations.literal: Hui said he did not understand current affairs; to employ him greatly would be inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said that Wang did not understand current affairs and that to employ him on a grand scale would be unwise.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎章辟光上言，岐王顥宜遷居外邸，皇太后怒，帝令治其離間之罪。

translations.literal: Editorial Assistant Zhang Boguang submitted that Prince Qi Hao ought to move to an outer residence; the Empress Dowager was angry, and the emperor ordered prosecution for the crime of sowing discord.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial assistant Zhang Boguang submitted a memorial saying Prince Qi should move to an outer residence; the empress dowager was incensed, and the emperor ordered him prosecuted for sowing discord.

sentences.zh: 安石謂無罪，誨請下辟光吏，不從，遂上疏劾安石曰：「大奸似忠，大佞似信，安石外示樸野，中藏巧詐，陛下悅其才辨而委任之。

translations.literal: Anshi said there was no crime; Hui asked that Boguang be handed to the officials for prosecution—not granted. He then submitted an impeachment of Anshi, saying, "Great villainy resembles loyalty; great sycophancy resembles trustworthiness. Anshi outwardly shows simplicity and rusticity while inwardly harboring craft and deceit. Your Majesty delights in his talent and eloquence and entrusts him.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi argued he was guiltless; Hui asked that Boguang be handed over to the judicial authorities—the request was denied. He then submitted a memorial impeaching Anshi: "The greatest villainy wears the mask of loyalty; the greatest sycophancy masquerades as sincerity. Anshi appears plain and rustic without while concealing craft and deceit within. Your Majesty delights in his talent and eloquence and has entrusted him with power.

sentences.zh: 安石初無遠略，惟務改作立異，罔上欺下，文言飾非，誤天下蒼生，必斯人也。

translations.literal: Anshi from the start had no far-reaching design; he only strove for reform and novelty, deceived above and cheated below, used elegant words to adorn error—he who will mislead the common people under Heaven must be this man.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi had no long-term vision from the start; he cared only for novelty and change, deceiving those above and misleading those below, dressing error in elegant words—if anyone is to lead the common people of the realm astray, it will be this man.

sentences.zh: 如久居廟堂，必無安靜之理。

translations.literal: If he long dwells in the hall of government, there will surely be no reason for tranquility.
translations.idiomatic: If he remains long in the seat of government, the realm will know no peace.

sentences.zh: 辟光之謀，本安石及呂惠卿所導。

translations.literal: Boguang's scheme originally was directed by Anshi and Lü Huiqing.
translations.idiomatic: Boguang's scheme had been instigated by Anshi and Lü Huiqing.

sentences.zh: 辟光揚言：『朝廷若深罪我，我終不置此二人。』

translations.literal: Boguang proclaimed publicly: "If the court deeply punishes me, I will never let these two men off."
translations.idiomatic: Boguang declared publicly, "If the court punishes me severely, I will never let these two men go."

sentences.zh: 故力加營救。

translations.literal: Therefore [Anshi] exerted himself forcefully to rescue [him].
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Anshi exerted himself mightily to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 願察於隱伏，質之士論，然後知臣言之當否。」

translations.literal: I wish that You examine what is hidden, verify with the judgment of scholar-officials, and then know whether my words are correct."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty probe what lies hidden and test my words against public opinion among scholar-officials—then you will know whether I speak rightly."

sentences.zh: 帝方注倚安石，還其章。

translations.literal: The emperor was then relying on Anshi and returned his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then placing his trust in Anshi and returned the memorial unacted upon.

sentences.zh: 誨求去，帝謂曾公亮曰：「若出誨，恐安石不自安。」

translations.literal: Hui asked to leave; the emperor said to Zeng Gongliang, "If Hui is sent out, I fear Anshi will not feel at ease."
translations.idiomatic: Hui asked to be dismissed; the emperor said to Zeng Gongliang, "If Hui is sent out, I fear Anshi will take it amiss."

sentences.zh: 安石曰：「臣以身許國，陛下處之有義，臣何敢以形跡自嫌，苟為去就。」

translations.literal: Anshi said, "I give my person to the state; if Your Majesty disposes of matters with justice, how dare I shrink from appearance and avoid coming or going casually?"
translations.idiomatic: Anshi said, "I have pledged my life to the state; if Your Majesty acts with justice, how dare I shrink from appearances or fuss over comings and goings?"

sentences.zh: 乃出誨知鄧州。

translations.literal: Hui was then sent out as prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was then sent out as prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 蘇頌當制，公亮謂之曰：「辟光治平四年上書時，安石在金陵，惠卿監杭州酒稅，安得而教之？」

translations.literal: Su Song was to draft the appointment edict; Gongliang said to him, "When Boguang submitted his memorial in the fourth year of Zhiping, Anshi was in Jinling and Huiqing was supervising the wine tax in Hangzhou—how could they have instructed him?"
translations.idiomatic: Su Song was assigned to draft the appointment edict; Gongliang said to him, "When Boguang submitted his memorial in the fourth year of Zhiping, Anshi was in Jinling and Huiqing was supervising the wine tax in Hangzhou—how could they have coached him?"

sentences.zh: 故制詞云：「黨小人交譖之言，肆罔上無根之語。」

translations.literal: Therefore the edict text read: "Favoring the slander of petty men, he wantonly used groundless words to deceive the sovereign above.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly the edict read, "He indulged the slander of petty men and wantonly spread baseless words to deceive the sovereign."

sentences.zh: 制出，帝以咎頌，以公亮之言告，乃知辟光治平時自言他事，非此也。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, the emperor blamed Song; when Gongliang's words were told him, he then learned that Boguang in the Zhiping era had spoken of other matters on his own—not this one.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued, the emperor blamed Song; after Gongliang's account was reported to him, he learned that during the Zhiping era Boguang had spoken on his own of other matters—not this one.

sentences.zh: 誨之將有言也，司馬光勸止之，誨曰：「安石雖有時名，然好執偏見，輕信奸回，喜人佞己。

translations.literal: When Hui was about to speak, Sima Guang advised him to stop; Hui said, "Although Anshi has a reputation of the times, he loves holding to partial views, lightly trusts wicked deceivers, and delights in having flatterers agree with himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Hui was about to speak out, Sima Guang urged him to hold back; Hui said, "Anshi may enjoy a reputation in his own time, but he clings to partial views, trusts wicked deceivers too readily, and delights in men who flatter him.

sentences.zh: 聽其言則美，施於用則疏；

translations.literal: Listen to his words and they are fine; apply them in practice and they are loose and flawed;
translations.idiomatic: His words sound fine in the hearing, but put into practice they prove unsound;

sentences.zh: 置諸宰輔，天下必受其禍。

translations.literal: set him among chief ministers and all under Heaven will surely suffer his calamity.
translations.idiomatic: place him among the chief ministers and the realm will surely suffer for it.

sentences.zh: 且上新嗣位，所與朝夕圖議者，二三執政而已，苟非其人，將敗國事。

translations.literal: Moreover the new sovereign has just succeeded; those with whom he daily plots and deliberates are only two or three chief ministers—if they are not the right men, state affairs will be ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the new sovereign has only just acceded; those with whom he deliberates day and night are no more than two or three chief ministers—if they are not the right men, the nation's business will be ruined.

sentences.zh: 此乃腹心之疾，救之惟恐不逮，顧可緩耶？」

translations.literal: This is a disease of the heart and belly—one saves it only fearing one will not arrive in time; how can one be slow?"
translations.idiomatic: This is a disease at the heart of the state—we must treat it before it is too late; how can we afford to delay?"

sentences.zh: 誨既斥，安石益橫。

translations.literal: Once Hui was dismissed, Anshi grew all the more overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hui was dismissed, Anshi grew all the more overbearing.

sentences.zh: 光由是服誨之先見，自以為不及也。

translations.literal: Guang thereby came to admire Hui's foresight and considered himself not equal to him.
translations.idiomatic: Guang came thereby to admire Hui's foresight and considered himself his inferior.

sentences.zh: 明年，改知河南，命未下而寢疾矣。

translations.literal: The next year he was changed to prefect of Henan; before the order was issued he fell seriously ill.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was reassigned as prefect of Henan, but before the order was issued he fell gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 旋提舉崇福宮，以疾表求致仕曰：「臣本無宿疾，醫者用術乖方，妄投湯劑，率任情意，差之指下，禍延四支。

translations.literal: Soon he was made promoter of Chongfu Palace; citing illness he submitted a request to retire, saying, "Your subject originally had no chronic illness; physicians used methods contrary to the proper course, recklessly administering decoctions, acting entirely by whim—a slight error at the fingertip, calamity spread to the four limbs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made promoter of Chongfu Palace; citing illness he submitted a request to retire, saying, "Your subject had no chronic ailment originally, but physicians applied the wrong methods and recklessly administered decoctions according to whim—a slight error at the fingertip, and calamity spread to all four limbs.

sentences.zh: 一身之微，固無足恤，奈九族之託何！」

translations.literal: The slightness of one body—of course not worth grieving; but what of the trust of the nine clans!"
translations.idiomatic: One body is a small thing and scarcely worth grieving over—but what of the charge entrusted to the nine clans!"

sentences.zh: 蓋以身疾諭朝政也。

translations.literal: This was using bodily illness to instruct on court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was using his bodily illness as an allegory for the state of court governance.

sentences.zh: 誨三居言責，皆以彈奏大臣而去，一時推其鯁直。

translations.literal: Three times Hui occupied the duty of speech and each time departed through impeaching chief ministers; for a time people praised his unyielding uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: Three times Hui held the duty of remonstrance and each time left office after impeaching chief ministers; for a time men praised his unyielding integrity.

sentences.zh: 居病困，猶旦夕憤歎，以天下事為憂。

translations.literal: While dwelling in severe illness, he still morning and evening sighed in anger, taking affairs under Heaven as his worry.
translations.idiomatic: Even in grave illness he still grieved and sighed morning and night, bearing the affairs of the realm on his mind.

sentences.zh: 既革，司馬光往省之，至則目已瞑。

translations.literal: When his condition turned critical, Sima Guang went to visit him; when he arrived, Hui's eyes were already closed.
translations.idiomatic: When his condition turned critical, Sima Guang went to visit him; when he arrived, Hui's eyes were already shut.

sentences.zh: 聞光哭，蹶然而起，張目強視曰：「天下事尚可為，君實勉之。」

translations.literal: Hearing Guang weep, he jolted upright, opened his eyes and forced himself to look, saying, "Affairs under Heaven can still be done—Junshi, exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing Guang weep, he jolted upright, opened his eyes with effort, and said, "The affairs of the realm can still be set right—Junshi, press on."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「更有以見屬乎？」

translations.literal: Guang said, "Is there anything further you would entrust to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Guang said, "Is there anything more you would entrust to me?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「無有。」

translations.literal: He said, "Nothing."
translations.idiomatic: He said, "Nothing."

sentences.zh: 遂卒，年五十八，海內聞者痛惜之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he died, aged fifty-eight; those who heard throughout the realm grieved and lamented him.
translations.idiomatic: He then died, at fifty-eight; all who heard grieved for him throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 元祐初，呂大防、范純仁、劉摯表其忠，詔贈通議大夫，以其子由庚為太常寺太祝。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanyou, Lü Dafang, Fan Chunren, and Liu Zhe memorialized his loyalty; an edict posthumously granted him General of Promotion of Righteousness and made his son Yougeng a senior temple warden of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Yuanyou era, Lü Dafang, Fan Chunren, and Liu Zhe memorialized his loyalty; an edict posthumously granted him the title General of Promotion of Righteousness and appointed his son Yougeng senior temple warden in the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 自誨罷去，御史劉述、劉琦、錢顗皆以言安石被黜。

translations.literal: From the time Hui was dismissed, Censors Liu Shu, Liu Qi, and Qian Yi were all demoted for speaking against Anshi.
translations.idiomatic: After Hui's dismissal, the censors Liu Shu, Liu Qi, and Qian Yi were all demoted for speaking against Anshi.

sentences.zh: 劉述，字孝叔，湖州人。

translations.literal: Liu Shu, styled Xiaoshu, was a native of Huzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shu, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshu, came from Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，為御史臺主簿，知溫、耀、真三州，提點江西刑獄，累官都官員外郎，六年不奏考功課。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served as chief clerk of the Censorate, was prefect of Wen, Yao, and Zhen prefectures, intendant of judicial affairs in Jiangxi, and by accumulated posts reached Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice; for six years he did not submit merit-and-demerit reports for the merit review.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served as chief clerk of the censorate, was prefect of Wen, Yao, and Zhen, served as judicial intendant for Jiangxi, rose by accumulated posts to vice director of the ministry of justice, and for six years did not submit his annual merit review.

sentences.zh: 知審官院胡宿言其沉靜有守，特遷兵部員外郎，改荊湖南北、京西路轉運使，再以覃恩遷刑部郎中。

translations.literal: Hu Su, who managed the Court of Review, said he was calm and steadfast; he was specially promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of War, transferred to be transport commissioner for Jinghu South-North and Jingxi circuits, and again, through a grace edict, promoted to Director of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Su of the Court of Review praised his calm integrity, and he was specially promoted to vice director of the ministry of war, made transport commissioner for the Jinghu and Jingxi circuits, and later advanced through a grace edict to director of the ministry of justice.

sentences.zh: 神宗立，召為侍御史知雜事，又十一年不奏課。

translations.literal: When Shenzong ascended the throne, he was summoned as supervising censor with charge of miscellaneous affairs; again for eleven years he did not submit merit reviews.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenzong came to the throne, he was summoned as supervising censor in charge of mixed duties, and again for eleven years he filed no annual merit review.

sentences.zh: 帝知其久次，授吏部郎中。

translations.literal: The emperor knew he had long remained in rank and appointed him Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing he had long remained at the same rank, the emperor appointed him director of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 嘗言去奢當自後宮始，章辟光宜誅，高居簡宜黜，張方平不當參大政，王拱辰不當除宣徽使。

translations.literal: He once said that cutting extravagance should begin with the inner palace; Zhang Biguang deserved execution, Gao Jujian deserved dismissal, Zhang Fangping should not participate in great governance, and Wang Gongchen should not be appointed Commissioner of the Xuanhui Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He once argued that curbing luxury should start in the inner palace, that Zhang Biguang deserved death, Gao Jujian deserved removal, that Zhang Fangping should not take part in high policy, and that Wang Gongchen should not be made commissioner of the Xuanhui Guard.

sentences.zh: 皆不報。

translations.literal: None received response.
translations.idiomatic: None of these memorials received a reply.

sentences.zh: 滕甫為中丞，述將論之。

translations.literal: When Teng Fu was censor-in-chief, Shu was about to memorialize against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Teng Fu served as censor-in-chief, Shu prepared to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 甫聞，先請對。

translations.literal: Fu heard this and first requested a private audience.
translations.idiomatic: Fu heard of it and first asked for a private audience with the emperor.

sentences.zh: 甫退，述乃言甫為言官無所發明，且擿其隱慝。

translations.literal: After Fu withdrew, Shu then said that Fu as a remonstrance officer had made no discoveries and moreover exposed his hidden wrongs.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu withdrew, Shu said that Fu, as a remonstrance officer, had produced nothing of substance and went on to expose his hidden misconduct.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「甫遇事輒爭，裨益甚多，但外人不知耳。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Fu whenever he encounters affairs always contends—he benefits things greatly, but outsiders do not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Fu contends over every matter that comes before him and does the court great good, though outsiders do not know it.

sentences.zh: 甫談卿美不輟口，卿無言也。」

translations.literal: Fu speaks of your virtues without cease—say no more."
translations.idiomatic: Fu never stops praising your virtues—say no more."

sentences.zh: 王安石參知政事，帝下詔專令中丞舉御史，不限官高卑。

translations.literal: When Wang Anshi became Vice Grand Councilor, the emperor issued an edict charging the censor-in-chief alone to recommend censors, with no limit on rank high or low.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Anshi became vice grand councilor, the emperor issued an edict giving the censor-in-chief sole authority to recommend censors, with no restriction on rank.

sentences.zh: 趙抃爭之，弗得。

translations.literal: Zhao Bian contested this but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Bian objected but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 述言：「舊制，舉御史官，須中行員外郎至太常博士，資任須實歷通判，又必翰林眾學士與本臺丞雜互舉。

translations.literal: Shu said: "Under the old system, those recommended as censorial officials had to be from Vice Director in the Secretariat-Chancellery track to Doctor of the Grand Imperial Sacrifice; qualifications required actual service as vice-prefect, and furthermore Hanlin academicians and this office's vice commissioners had to recommend in mixed rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Shu said, "Under the old system, censorial nominees had to hold ranks from vice director in the secretariat-chancellery track down to doctor of the grand imperial sacrifice, with actual experience as vice-prefect; and Hanlin academicians and the censorate's own vice commissioners had to recommend them in mixed rotation.

sentences.zh: 蓋眾議僉舉，則各務盡心，不容有偏蔽私愛之患。

translations.literal: For when all deliberated and jointly recommended, each would exhaust his heart, and partiality and private favoritism could not arise.
translations.idiomatic: When many voices joined in recommendation, each would do his utmost and there would be no room for bias or private favor.

sentences.zh: 今專委中丞，則愛憎在於一己。

translations.literal: Now if entrusted solely to the censor-in-chief, likes and dislikes rest in one man alone.
translations.idiomatic: Now, if the choice rests with the censor-in-chief alone, likes and dislikes will be his alone.

sentences.zh: 若一一得人，猶不至生事；

translations.literal: If one and all were well chosen, it might not yet lead to trouble;
translations.idiomatic: If every appointee were the right man, trouble might still be avoided;

sentences.zh: 萬一非其人，將受權臣屬託，自立黨援，不附己者得以中傷，媒蘖誣陷，其弊不一。

translations.literal: but if by any chance the wrong men were chosen, they would receive commissions from powerful ministers, establish factional support, and those not attached to them could be slandered and falsely implicated by insinuation—the abuses would be manifold.
translations.idiomatic: but if even one unworthy man were chosen, he would take orders from powerful ministers, build a faction of his own, and those who would not join him could be slandered and framed by whispered accusation—the abuses would be many.

sentences.zh: 夫變更法度，其事不輕，而止是參知政事二人，同書劄子。

translations.literal: Now to change laws and institutions is no light matter, yet this was merely two Vice Grand Councilors jointly signing a memorandum.
translations.idiomatic: To change laws and institutions is no small matter, yet here only two vice grand councilors signed a joint memorandum.

sentences.zh: 且宰相富弼暫謁告，曾公亮已入朝，臺官今不闕人，何至急疾如此！

translations.literal: Moreover the chief councilor Fu Bi was temporarily on leave, Zeng Gongliang had already entered court, and the censorate is not now short of men—why press forward so urgently!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Chief Councilor Fu Bi was temporarily on leave, Zeng Gongliang had already taken his seat at court, and the censorate is not short-handed—why the sudden haste!

sentences.zh: 願收還前旨，俟弼出，與公亮同議，然後行之。」

translations.literal: I beg that the previous directive be withdrawn; wait until Bi emerges, discuss together with Gongliang, and then implement it."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the earlier order be withdrawn, and that after Bi returns you discuss the matter with Gongliang and only then put it into effect."

sentences.zh: 弗聽。

translations.literal: Not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: His plea went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 述兼判刑部，安石爭謀殺刑名，述不以為是。

translations.literal: Shu additionally served as judicial commissioner of the Ministry of Justice; Anshi contended over the legal classification of premeditated murder, and Shu did not consider him correct.
translations.idiomatic: Shu also served as judicial commissioner of the ministry of justice. Anshi pressed his view on the legal classification of premeditated murder, and Shu rejected it.

sentences.zh: 及敕下，述封還中書，奏執不已。

translations.literal: When the edict was issued, Shu sealed it and returned it to the Secretariat, memorializing and holding to his view without cease.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict came down, Shu sealed it and sent it back to the Secretariat, memorializing again and again in defense of his position.

sentences.zh: 安石白帝，詔開封府推官王克臣劾述罪。

translations.literal: Anshi reported to the emperor, and an edict ordered Kaifeng investigating officer Wang Kezhen to impeach Shu for offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi reported to the emperor, and an edict ordered Wang Kezhen, investigating officer of the Kaifeng prefecture, to impeach Shu.

sentences.zh: 於是述率御史劉琦、錢顗共上疏曰：

translations.literal: Thereupon Shu led censors Liu Qi and Qian Yi in jointly submitting a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Shu, together with censors Liu Qi and Qian Yi, submitted a joint memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 「安石執政以來，未逾數月，中外人情囂然胥動。

translations.literal: "Since Anshi took power, in not yet a few months, feelings inside and outside have been in uproar and all stirred.
translations.idiomatic: "Since Anshi took power, in less than a few months feeling inside and outside the court has been in uproar.

sentences.zh: 蓋以專肆胸臆，輕易憲度，無忌憚之心故也。

translations.literal: This is because he indulges his own breast and belly, lightly changes constitutional norms, and has a heart without fear or restraint.
translations.idiomatic: This is because he follows his own whim, treats the laws lightly, and acts without fear or restraint.

sentences.zh: 陛下任賢求治，常若饑渴，故置安石政府。

translations.literal: Your Majesty appoints the worthy and seeks good order, always as if hungry and thirsty—therefore you placed Anshi in the government.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty seeks worthy men and good government with the eagerness of hunger and thirst, and so you placed Anshi in office.

sentences.zh: 必欲致時如唐、虞，而反操管、商權詐之術，規以取媚。

translations.literal: You surely wished to bring the age to be like Tang and Yu, yet he instead wields the arts of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang—craft and deceit—scheming to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: You meant to bring the age to the level of Tang and Yu, yet he instead practices the cunning arts of Guan Zhong and Shang Yang, scheming only to please.

sentences.zh: 遂與陳升之合謀，侵三司利柄，取為己功；

translations.literal: He then joined Chen Shengzhi in conspiracy, encroaching on the Three Fiscal Departments' powers of profit and seizing them as his own merit;
translations.idiomatic: He then conspired with Chen Shengzhi to seize the revenue powers of the Three Fiscal Departments and claim the credit for himself;

sentences.zh: 開局設官，用八人者分行天下，驚駭物聽，動搖人心。

translations.literal: establishing offices and appointing officials, using eight men to travel separately through the realm, startling all who heard and shaking people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: opening new bureaus, appointing officials, and sending eight men out across the empire—shocking all who heard of it and unsettling the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 去年因許遵文過飾非，妄議自首按問之法，安石任一偏之見，改立新議，以害天下大公。

translations.literal: Last year on account of Xu Zun's whitewashing faults and covering errors, he recklessly debated the law on voluntary confession and interrogation; Anshi indulged one partial view, changed and established a new proposal, harming the great public justice of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Last year, building on Xu Zun's glossing over faults, he rashly proposed changes to the law on voluntary confession and interrogation; Anshi indulged this one-sided view, overturned established practice, and harmed the public good of the realm.

sentences.zh: 章辟光獻岐邸遷外之說，疏間骨肉，罪不容誅。

translations.literal: Zhang Biguang offered the proposal of removing the Prince of Qi to an outer post, estranging flesh and bone—the crime brooks no sparing of execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Biguang urged that the Prince of Qi be sent away from court, sowing discord between kin—a crime that deserved death.

sentences.zh: 呂誨等連章論奏，乞加竄逐。

translations.literal: Lu Hui and others sent successive memorials arguing for prosecution, begging that he be harshly exiled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hui and others submitted memorial after memorial demanding that he be punished and banished.

sentences.zh: 陛下雖許其請，安石獨進瞽言，熒惑聖聽。

translations.literal: Though Your Majesty granted their request, Anshi alone advanced blind words and confused the sage ear.
translations.idiomatic: Though Your Majesty agreed to their request, Anshi alone spoke blind counsel and misled Your Majesty's judgment.

sentences.zh: 陛下以為愛己，隱忍不行。

translations.literal: Your Majesty, thinking he loved yourself, forbore and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, believing that he was acting out of personal loyalty, held back and did nothing.

sentences.zh: 先朝所立制度，自宜世世子孫，守而勿失；

translations.literal: The institutions established by the previous court ought naturally to be guarded by generation after generation of descendants and not lost;
translations.idiomatic: The institutions of the previous reign ought to be preserved by every generation and never abandoned;

sentences.zh: 乃欲事事更張，廢而不用。

translations.literal: yet he wishes to change everything and abolish what should not be used.
translations.idiomatic: yet he would change everything and cast aside what should be kept.

sentences.zh: 安石自應舉歷官，尊尚堯、舜之道，以倡率學者，故士人之心靡不歸向，謂之為賢。

translations.literal: From his examination through his official career, Anshi revered the Way of Yao and Shun to lead scholars—therefore scholars' hearts none failed to turn toward him, calling him worthy.
translations.idiomatic: From the examinations through his official career, Anshi upheld the way of Yao and Shun and led the scholars, so that men of learning all turned to him and called him worthy.

sentences.zh: 陛下亦聞而知之，遂正位公府。

translations.literal: Your Majesty too heard and knew it, and thus elevated him to the chief seat of the government.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty heard the same and, knowing it, raised him to the highest office.

sentences.zh: 遭時得君如此之專，乃首建財利之議，務為容悅，言行乖戾，一至於此。

translations.literal: Meeting the time and gaining the ruler with such exclusive favor, yet he first established proposals for profit and revenue, striving to please—words and acts at odds, reaching even to this.
translations.idiomatic: Given such exclusive favor from the throne, he ought to have served the age; instead he led with schemes for profit, striving only to please—so far have his words and deeds diverged.

sentences.zh: 剛狠自任，則又甚焉。

translations.literal: His obstinate harshness and self-assumption go even further.
translations.idiomatic: His obstinacy and self-will go further still.

sentences.zh: 姦詐專權之人，豈宜處之廟堂，以亂國紀！

translations.literal: A man of treachery, deceit, and monopolized power—how should he be placed in the temple hall to disorder the nation's statutes!
translations.idiomatic: How can a man so treacherous, so deceitful, and so hungry for power be kept in the halls of government to disorder the laws of the state!

sentences.zh: 願早罷逐，以慰安天下元元之心。

translations.literal: We beg early dismissal and expulsion, to comfort and settle the hearts of the myriad common people under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: We beg that he be removed at once, to reassure the hearts of the common people throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 曾公亮位居丞弼，不能竭忠許國，反有畏避之意，陰自結援以固寵，久妨賢路，亦宜斥免。

translations.literal: Zeng Gongliang occupies the seat of chief assistant, yet cannot exhaust loyalty in serving the state; instead he has thoughts of fear and avoidance, secretly forming alliances to secure favor—long obstructing the path of worthies—he too should be expelled and removed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Gongliang sits among the chief ministers yet fails to serve the state with full loyalty; instead he shrinks back in fear, secretly builds alliances to protect his position, and long blocks the path of worthy men—he too should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 趙抃則括囊拱手，但務依違大臣，事君豈當如是！」

translations.literal: Zhao Bian ties his purse and folds his hands, only striving to waver along with great ministers—is serving the ruler right to be thus!"
translations.idiomatic: As for Zhao Bian, he keeps his purse shut and his hands folded, doing nothing but drift with the great ministers—is that how one should serve the ruler!"

sentences.zh: 疏上，安石奏先貶琦、顗監處、衢州鹽務。

translations.literal: When the memorial went up, Anshi memorialized that Qi and Yi first be demoted to supervise salt affairs in Chuzhou and Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Anshi proposed that Qi and Yi be demoted first to supervise salt affairs at Chuzhou and Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 公亮疑太重，安石曰：「蔣之奇亦降監，當從之。」

translations.literal: Gongliang thought this too heavy; Anshi said: "Jiang Zhiqi was also demoted to supervisor—this should follow suit."
translations.idiomatic: Gongliang thought the penalty too harsh. Anshi said, "Jiang Zhiqi was also demoted to a supervisory post—we should follow that precedent."

sentences.zh: 司馬光乃上疏曰：「臣聞孔子曰：『守道不如守官。』

translations.literal: Sima Guang then submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant hears Confucius said: 'Upholding the Way is not as good as upholding one's office.'
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang then submitted a memorial saying, "I have heard Confucius say, 'To uphold the Way is not as good as to uphold one's office.'

sentences.zh: 孟子曰：『有言責者，不得其言則去。』

translations.literal: Mencius said: 'One charged with speech who does not obtain his speech then departs.'
translations.idiomatic: Mencius said, 'One whose duty is to speak, if he cannot speak as he ought, should leave.'

sentences.zh: 此古今通義，人臣之大節也。

translations.literal: This is the common principle of past and present—the great integrity of a minister.
translations.idiomatic: This is the enduring principle of all ages—the great duty of a minister.

sentences.zh: 彼謀殺已傷自首刑名，天下皆知其非。

translations.literal: That premeditated murder matter has already harmed the legal term for voluntary confession—all under Heaven know it is wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The change to the law on premeditated murder and voluntary confession is already known throughout the realm to be wrong.

sentences.zh: 朝廷既違眾議而行之，又以守官之臣而罪之，臣恐失天下之心也。

translations.literal: The court having already gone against collective deliberation to implement it, and now furthermore punishing ministers who uphold their office—your servant fears losing the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The court already overrode public opinion to enforce it, and now would punish ministers for doing their duty—I fear the realm will lose heart.

sentences.zh: 夫絏食鷹鸇者，求其鷙也，鷙而烹之，將安用哉！

translations.literal: Now one who feeds hawks and falcons with tied meat seeks their fierceness—if once fierce you cook them, of what use will they be!
translations.idiomatic: A man who feeds hawks and falcons on tied bait wants their fierceness—once they are fierce, if you cook them, what use are they!

sentences.zh: 今琦、顗所坐，不過疏直，乃以迕犯大臣，猥加譴謫，恐臣下自此以言為諱。

translations.literal: Now what Qi and Yi are guilty of is nothing beyond blunt straightforwardness—yet because they offended great ministers they were rashly punished and demoted; I fear ministers from this will take speech as taboo.
translations.idiomatic: Qi and Yi are guilty of nothing but blunt honesty, yet because they crossed powerful ministers they were harshly punished and demoted—I fear that from now on officials will shrink from speaking out.

sentences.zh: 乞還其本資，以靖群聽。」

translations.literal: I beg that their original rank be restored, to settle the ears of the multitude."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that their original ranks be restored, to quiet the alarm of the court."

sentences.zh: 不報。

translations.literal: No response.
translations.idiomatic: There was no reply.

sentences.zh: 開封獄具，述三問不承。

translations.literal: The Kaifeng prison case was complete; through three interrogations Shu did not confess.
translations.idiomatic: The Kaifeng investigation was concluded; through three interrogations Shu would not confess.

sentences.zh: 安石欲置之獄，光又與范純仁爭之，乃議貶為通判。

translations.literal: Anshi wished to imprison him; Guang again contended with Fan Chunren, and they then deliberated demoting him to vice-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi wanted him imprisoned; Guang again argued with Fan Chunren, and they finally agreed on demoting him to vice-prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝不許，以知江州。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit this and appointed him prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree and instead appointed him prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，提舉崇禧觀。

translations.literal: After a year, he was made superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was made superintendent of the Chongxi Abbey.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，紹興初，贈秘閣修撰。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-two; at the beginning of the Shaoxing era he was posthumously granted Secretariat Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-two. At the beginning of the Shaoxing era he was posthumously granted the title Secretariat Compiler.

sentences.zh: 劉琦，字公玉，宣城人。

translations.literal: Liu Qi, styled Gongyu, was a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qi, whose courtesy name was Gongyu, came from Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 博學強覽，立志峻潔。

translations.literal: Broadly learned with strong comprehension, he set his resolve high and pure.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly learned and quick to grasp what he read, he held himself to a stern and upright standard.

sentences.zh: 以都官員外郎通判歙州。

translations.literal: As Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice he served as vice-prefect of Shezhou.
translations.idiomatic: As vice director of the ministry of justice he served as vice-prefect of Shezhou.

sentences.zh: 召為侍御史，建言：「自城綏州，數致羌寇，宜棄之。」

translations.literal: Summoned as attendant censor, he offered advice: "Since fortifying Suizhou, we have repeatedly brought on Qiang raids—it should be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: Summoned as attendant censor, he memorialized, "Since Suizhou was fortified we have repeatedly provoked Qiang raids—it should be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 浙西開漕渠，役甚小，使者張大其事，以功遷官。

translations.literal: In western Zhejiang a transport canal was opened—the labor was very small, but the envoy inflated the matter and was promoted for merit.
translations.idiomatic: In western Zhejiang a transport canal was opened; the work was slight, but the envoy exaggerated it and was promoted for merit.

sentences.zh: 言者論其非，詔琦就劾，官吏人人惴恐。

translations.literal: Critics argued against this; an edict ordered Qi to go investigate—all officials were fearful in dread.
translations.idiomatic: Critics denounced the affair, and an edict ordered Qi to investigate on the spot; every official was terrified.

sentences.zh: 琦但按首謀二人而已。

translations.literal: Qi only prosecuted the two chief plotters, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Qi prosecuted only the two ringleaders and no one else.

sentences.zh: 既貶，通判鄧州而卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: After demotion, as vice-prefect of Dengzhou he died, age sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: After his demotion he served as vice-prefect of Dengzhou, where he died at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 錢顗，字安道，常州無錫人。

translations.literal: Qian Yi, styled Andao, was a native of Wuxi in Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yi, whose courtesy name was Andao, came from Wuxi in Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 初為寧海軍節度推官，守孫沔用威嚴為治，屬吏奔走聽命。

translations.literal: Initially he was military governorship investigating officer of Ninghai Army; the prefect Sun Yan governed through awesomeness and severity, and subordinate officials ran about obeying orders.
translations.idiomatic: He began as investigating officer under the Ninghai military governorship. The prefect Sun Yan ruled by fear, and his subordinates scurried to obey.

sentences.zh: 顗當官而行，無所容撓，遇不可，必爭之，由是獨見器重。

translations.literal: Yi conducted office and acted, brooking no bending; when he encountered what was not permissible he always contended—thereby alone winning heavy esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Yi did his duty without yielding; whenever he saw something wrong he fought it, and for this alone he won special respect.

sentences.zh: 知贛、烏程二縣，皆以治行聞。

translations.literal: As prefect of Gan and Wucheng counties, in both cases his governance and conduct were renowned.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Gan and Wucheng counties, he was known in both places for the quality of his administration.

sentences.zh: 治平末，以金部員外郎為殿中侍御史裏行。

translations.literal: At the end of the Zhiping era, as Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue he served as acting palace censor.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Zhiping era he served as acting palace censor while holding the rank of vice director of the ministry of revenue.

sentences.zh: 許遵議謀殺案問刑名，未定而入判大理，顗以為：「一人偏詞，不可以汨天下之法，遵所見迂執，不可以當刑法之任。」

translations.literal: Xu Zun debated the legal classification of a premeditated murder case; before it was decided he entered to judge at the Court of Judicial Review. Yi considered: "One man's partial words cannot muddy the laws of all under Heaven; Zun's views are cramped and obstinate—he cannot bear the burden of penal law."
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zun disputed the legal classification of a premeditated murder case and, before the issue was settled, was appointed to judge at the Court of Judicial Review. Yi argued, "One man's biased opinion must not cloud the law of the realm; Zun's views are narrow and stubborn, and he is unfit to bear responsibility for penal law."

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: Not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: His objection was not accepted.

sentences.zh: 二年而貶，將出臺，於眾中責同列孫昌齡曰：「平日士大夫未嘗知君名，徒以昔官金陵，媚事王安石，宛轉薦君，得為御史。

translations.literal: After two years he was demoted; about to leave the censorate, before the assembly he rebuked his colleague Sun Changling: "Ordinarily scholars never knew your name—you merely because you once held office at Jinling fawned on Wang Anshi and through roundabout recommendation got you made censor.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later he was demoted. As he was about to leave the censorate, he rebuked his colleague Sun Changling before the whole assembly: "Ordinary scholars never even knew your name. You merely fawned on Wang Anshi while serving at Jinling, and through backstairs recommendation won appointment as censor.

sentences.zh: 亦當少思執國，奈何專欲附會以求美官？

translations.literal: You should also give some thought to holding the state—why insist on currying favor to seek a fine office?
translations.idiomatic: You ought at least to think about the welfare of the state—why must you court favor only to win a better post?

sentences.zh: 顗今當遠竄，君自謂得策邪？

translations.literal: Yi now faces distant banishment—do you deem your strategy a success?
translations.idiomatic: I am now being sent into distant exile—do you think your strategy has succeeded?

sentences.zh: 我視君犬彘之不如也。」

translations.literal: I regard you as not equal to dogs and swine."
translations.idiomatic: In my eyes you are lower than dogs and swine."

sentences.zh: 即拂衣上馬去。

translations.literal: He immediately shook out his robe, mounted his horse, and departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that he shook out his robes, mounted his horse, and rode away.

sentences.zh: 後自衢徙秀州。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred from Quzhou to Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was transferred from Quzhou to Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 家貧母老，至丐貸親舊以給朝晡，而怡然無謫官之色。

translations.literal: His family was poor and his mother old; he even begged loans from kin and friends to supply morning and evening meals, yet was at ease without the look of one demoted.
translations.idiomatic: His family was poor and his mother elderly; he had to borrow from friends and relatives even for daily meals, yet he remained cheerful and showed none of the bitterness of exile.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾遺以詩，有「烏府先生鐵作肝」之句，世因目為「鐵肝御史」。

translations.literal: Su Shi sent him a poem with the line "The gentleman of the black office has a liver of iron"—the world therefore styled him the Iron-Liver Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi sent him a poem containing the line "The censor of the black office has a liver of iron," and men thereafter called him the Iron-Liver Censor.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十三。

translations.literal: He died at age fifty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-three.

sentences.zh: 鄭俠，字介夫，福州福清人。

translations.literal: Zheng Xia, styled Jiefu, was a native of Fuqing in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xia, whose courtesy name was Jiefu, came from Fuqing in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 治平中，隨父官江寧，閉戶苦學。

translations.literal: During Zhiping, following his father to office at Jiangning, he shut his doors and studied arduously.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhiping era he accompanied his father to a post at Jiangning, shut his doors, and studied with fierce dedication.

sentences.zh: 王安石知其名，邀與相見，稱獎之。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi knew his reputation, invited him to meet, and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi knew his name, invited him to an audience, and praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 進士高第，調光州司法參軍。

translations.literal: Graduating jinshi with high rank, he was assigned as legal aide of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination with high honors and was appointed legal aide in Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 安石居政府。

translations.literal: Anshi occupied the government.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was in power.

sentences.zh: 凡所施行，民間不以為便。

translations.literal: Whatever he implemented, the common people did not find convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever he put into effect, the people found burdensome.

sentences.zh: 光有疑獄，俠讞議傅奏，安石悉如其請。

translations.literal: Guangzhou had doubtful cases; Xia judged, deliberated, memorialized in relay—and Anshi granted all as he requested.
translations.idiomatic: When Guang Prefecture had doubtful cases, Xia reviewed them, drafted opinions, and forwarded memorials; Anshi approved every request.

sentences.zh: 俠感為知己，思欲盡忠。

translations.literal: Xia was moved and took him as a confidant, thinking to exhaust loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Xia was deeply moved, regarded him as a patron who understood him, and resolved to serve him with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，徑入都。

translations.literal: When his term expired, he went straight to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended, he went directly to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時初行試法之令，選人中式者超京官，安石欲使以是進，俠以未嘗習法辭。

translations.literal: At the time the trial-law edict had just been implemented—selectees who passed could leap to capital official rank; Anshi wished to advance him thereby, but Xia declined on grounds he had never studied law.
translations.idiomatic: The new law-examination decree had just taken effect, allowing successful candidates to leap to capital office; Anshi wanted to advance him by that route, but Xia declined on the ground that he had never studied law.

sentences.zh: 三往見之，問以所聞，對曰：「青苗、免役、保甲、市易數事，與邊鄙用兵，在俠心不能無區區也。」

translations.literal: Three times he went to see him; asked what he had heard, he replied: "The Green Sprouts loan program, labor-exemption tax, baojia system, market-trade office—these several matters, and military use on the frontier—in Xia's heart cannot be without small concerns."
translations.idiomatic: Three times he visited him. When Anshi asked what he had heard, he answered, "The Green Sprouts loans, the labor-exemption tax, the baojia system, the market-trade monopoly, and frontier warfare—I cannot pretend these give me no concern."

sentences.zh: 安石不答。

translations.literal: Anshi did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi made no answer.

sentences.zh: 俠退不復見，但數以書言法之為民害者。

translations.literal: Xia withdrew and did not meet again, but repeatedly by letter spoke of how the laws harmed the people.
translations.idiomatic: Xia withdrew and never visited again, but wrote letter after letter describing how the new laws harmed the people.

sentences.zh: 久之，監安上門。

translations.literal: After a long while, he was assigned to supervise the Anshang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he was appointed supervisor of the Anshang Gate.

sentences.zh: 安石雖不悅，猶使其子雱來，語以試法。

translations.literal: Though Anshi was displeased, he still sent his son Bian to speak with him about the law examination.
translations.idiomatic: Though displeased, Anshi still sent his son Wang Bian to discuss the law examination with him.

sentences.zh: 方置修經局，又欲辟為檢討，更命其客黎東美諭意，俠曰：「讀書無幾，不足以辱檢討。

translations.literal: Just as the Classics Revision Bureau was being established, he also wished to appoint Xia as collator; he further had his client Li Dongmei convey his intent. Xia said, "My reading has been slight—not enough to honor the post of collator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Classics Revision Bureau was being set up, Anshi also wanted to appoint Xia as a collator and sent his client Li Dongmei to explain his intent. Xia replied, "I have read too little to deserve the title of collator.

sentences.zh: 所以來，求執經相君門下耳。

translations.literal: The reason I came was simply to hold the classics and serve under the prime minister's gate.
translations.idiomatic: I came only to study the classics under the prime minister's tutelage.

sentences.zh: 而相君發言持論，無非以官爵為先，所以待士者亦淺矣。

translations.literal: Yet in the prime minister's every utterance and argument, nothing comes before office and rank; the way he treats scholars is likewise shallow.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in everything the prime minister says and argues, office and rank come first; the way he treats men of learning is shallow as well.

sentences.zh: 果欲援俠而成就之，取其所獻利民便物之事，行其一二，使進而無愧，不亦善乎？」

translations.literal: If you truly wish to support Xia and bring him to success, take the things he has submitted that benefit the people and ease their lives, carry out one or two of them, and let him advance without shame—is that not good?"
translations.idiomatic: If you truly mean to help Xia and see him succeed, take the proposals he has offered for the people's benefit, put one or two into practice, and let him rise without shame—would that not be better?"

sentences.zh: 是時，免役法出，民商咸以為苦，雖負水、捨髮、擔粥、提茶之屬，非納錢者不得販鬻。

translations.literal: At that time the labor-exemption law had been issued; commoners and merchants alike found it bitter—even water carriers, barbers, porridge bearers, and tea carriers and the like could not sell their goods unless they paid fees.
translations.idiomatic: By then the labor-exemption tax had been promulgated, and townspeople and merchants alike found it oppressive—even water carriers, barbers, porridge sellers, and tea hawkers could not trade unless they paid fees.

sentences.zh: 稅務索市利錢，其末或重於本，商人至以死爭，如是者不一。

translations.literal: Tax offices demanded market-profit money; the tax on the margin sometimes exceeded the principal, and merchants even fought to the death over it—such cases were not few.
translations.idiomatic: Tax offices demanded market-profit levies that sometimes exceeded the cost of the goods themselves, and merchants even fought to the death over them—such cases were countless.

sentences.zh: 俠因東美列其事。

translations.literal: Xia, through Dongmei, set forth these matters.
translations.idiomatic: Xia reported these abuses to Anshi through Li Dongmei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，詔小夫裨販者免征，商之重者十損其七，他皆無所行。

translations.literal: Before long, an edict exempted petty peddlers from the tax; for heavier merchants the levy was reduced by seven-tenths, and the other measures were not enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict exempted petty street vendors from the tax, cut the heaviest merchant levies by seven-tenths, and left the other measures unenforced.

sentences.zh: 是時，自熙寧六年七月不雨，至於七年之三月，人無生意。

translations.literal: At that time, from the seventh month of the sixth year of Xining there had been no rain until the third month of the seventh year, and people had no will to live.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh month of the sixth year of Xining until the third month of the seventh year, no rain fell, and the people lost all hope of living.

sentences.zh: 東北流民，每風沙霾曀，扶攜塞道，羸瘠愁苦，身無完衣。

translations.literal: Refugees from the northeast, whenever wind and dust darkened the sky, filled the roads supporting one another—emaciated, anguished, without a whole garment on their bodies.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from the northeast clogged the roads whenever wind and dust blotted out the sky—emaciated, wretched, without a whole garment to their names.

sentences.zh: 並城民買麻糝麥麩，合米為糜，或茹木實草根，至身被鎖械，而負瓦楬木，賣以償官，累累不絕。

translations.literal: People in the capital bought hemp bran and wheat bran and mixed them with rice into gruel, or ate tree fruit and grass roots; some even wore shackles while carrying tiles and timber to sell in payment to the government—an unbroken stream of such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Capital residents bought hemp bran and wheat bran to mix with rice into gruel, or lived on wild fruit and grass roots; some wore shackles even as they hauled tiles and timber to sell and pay the state—such scenes never ceased.

sentences.zh: 俠知安石不可諫，悉繪所見為圖，奏疏詣閤門，不納。

translations.literal: Xia knew Anshi could not be remonstrated with; he fully painted what he had seen into a picture, submitted a memorial at the Gate of Receiving Instruction, and it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing Anshi would not heed remonstrance, Xia painted everything he had witnessed, brought a memorial to the Gate of Receiving Instruction, and was turned away.

sentences.zh: 乃假稱密急，發馬遞上之銀臺司。

translations.literal: He then falsely claimed urgent secrecy and dispatched it by courier horse to the Yintai Office.
translations.idiomatic: He then falsely marked it as a secret emergency and sent it by courier to the Yintai Office.

sentences.zh: 其略云：

translations.literal: Its gist ran:
translations.idiomatic: The memorial in essence said:

sentences.zh: 「去年大蝗，秋冬亢旱，麥苗焦枯，五種不入，群情懼死；

translations.literal: "Last year there was a great locust plague; in autumn and winter drought was severe; wheat seedlings withered and burned; the five grains did not enter the granaries; the people's hearts fear death;
translations.idiomatic: "Last year brought a great locust plague; through autumn and winter drought raged; wheat withered in the fields; the five grains failed; the people live in dread of death;

sentences.zh: 方春斬伐，竭澤而漁，草木魚鱉，亦莫生遂。

translations.literal: now in spring they cut and fell everything, draining the marsh to catch fish—plants, fish, and turtles alike cannot survive and thrive.
translations.idiomatic: now in spring they strip the land bare and drain every pool for fish—grass, trees, fish, and turtles alike cannot live on;

sentences.zh: 災患之來，莫之或禦。

translations.literal: when calamity comes, none can ward it off.
translations.idiomatic: when disaster strikes, none can hold it back.

sentences.zh: 願陛下開倉廩，賑貧乏，取有司掊克不道之政，一切罷去。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will open the granaries, relieve the poor and destitute, and take every oppressive and unjust policy of the officials and abolish it all.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to open the granaries, relieve the destitute, and abolish every oppressive and unjust measure of the officials.

sentences.zh: 冀下召和氣，上應天心，延萬姓垂死之命。

translations.literal: I hope below to summon harmonious qi and above to answer Heaven's heart, prolonging the lives of the myriad people on the brink of death.
translations.idiomatic: May this summon harmony below and answer Heaven above, and prolong the lives of countless people already at death's door.

sentences.zh: 今臺諫充位，左右輔弼又皆貪猥近利，使夫抱道懷識之士，皆不欲與之言，陛下以爵祿名器，駕馭天下忠賢，而使人如此，甚非宗廟社稷之福也。

translations.literal: Now the censorial and remonstrance officials merely fill their posts, and the ministers left and right are again all greedy, base, and near-sighted in profit, so that men who embrace the Way and harbor talent all refuse to speak with them. Your Majesty uses titles, stipends, and honors to drive the loyal and worthy of the empire—yet to make men like this is greatly not the blessing of the ancestral temples and altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Today the censorial and remonstrance offices are filled with placeholders, and the ministers at your side are greedy, base men chasing profit, so that worthy men who hold to the Way will not speak with them. Your Majesty governs the empire's loyal talent with rank and reward—yet to leave men such as these in power is no blessing to the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 竊聞南征北伐者，皆以其勝捷之勢、山川之形，為圖來獻，料無一人以天下之民質妻鬻子，斬桑壞舍，流離逃散，遑遑不給之狀上聞者。

translations.literal: I have heard that those campaigning south and north all submit maps showing their victorious momentum and the terrain of mountains and rivers; I expect not one person has reported to Your Majesty the condition of the empire's people—pledging wives and selling children, cutting mulberry trees and destroying houses, wandering in flight and scattering, anxious and without provision.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that every commander returning from southern and northern campaigns brings maps of victories and terrain; yet not one has reported how the people of the realm are pawning wives and selling children, cutting mulberry trees and tearing down homes, fleeing in desperation without enough to live on.

sentences.zh: 臣謹以逐日所見，繪成一圖，但經眼目，已可涕泣。

translations.literal: Your subject respectfully paints into one picture what he sees day by day; merely to pass it before the eyes already draws tears.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject has painted into one scroll what he sees each day; the sight alone is enough to weep.

sentences.zh: 而況有甚於此者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when there are things worse than this!
translations.idiomatic: And how much worse are the things not shown!

sentences.zh: 如陛下行臣之言，十日不雨，即乞斬臣宣德門外，以正欺君之罪。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty carries out your subject's words and there is no rain in ten days, then I beg to be executed outside the Xuande Gate to rectify the crime of deceiving the ruler."
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty acts on this memorial and no rain falls within ten days, I ask to be executed outside the Xuande Gate for the crime of deceiving my sovereign."

sentences.zh: 疏奏，神宗反覆觀圖，長籲數四，袖以入。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Shenzong repeatedly examined the picture, sighed long four times, and put it in his sleeve as he entered.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Shenzong studied the picture again and again, sighed deeply four times, and carried it inside in his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 是夕，寢不能寐。

translations.literal: That night he could not sleep.
translations.idiomatic: That night he could not sleep.

sentences.zh: 翌日，命開封體放免行錢，三司察市易，司農發常平倉，三衛具熙河所用兵，諸路上民物流散之故。

translations.literal: The next day he ordered Kaifeng to suspend collection of transit exemption fees in practice, the Three Departments to investigate market-trade offices, the Directorate of Agriculture to release the Ever-Normal Granary stores, the Three Guard units to report troops used in Xihe, and the circuit intendants to explain why people and goods on the roads had scattered.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he ordered Kaifeng to stop collecting transit exemption fees in practice, the Three Departments to investigate the market-trade offices, the Directorate of Agriculture to open the Ever-Normal Granaries, the Three Guard units to account for troops used in Xihe, and circuit intendants to report why people and goods had scattered along the roads.

sentences.zh: 青苗、免役權息追呼，方田、保甲並罷，凡十有八事。

translations.literal: Green Sprouts and labor-exemption interest collections were temporarily halted, field-equalization and baojia were both abolished—in all eighteen measures.
translations.idiomatic: Green Sprouts and labor-exemption interest collections were suspended, and field-equalization and baojia were abolished—eighteen measures in all.

sentences.zh: 民間歡叫相賀。

translations.literal: Among the people there were shouts of joy and mutual congratulation.
translations.idiomatic: People in the streets shouted for joy and congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 又下責躬詔求言。

translations.literal: An edict of self-reproach was also issued inviting criticism.
translations.idiomatic: The throne also issued an edict of self-reproach inviting remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 越三日，大雨，遠近沾洽。

translations.literal: After three days, great rain fell, soaking near and far.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later heavy rain fell, soaking the land far and near.

sentences.zh: 輔臣入賀，帝示以俠所進圖狀，且責之，皆再拜謝。

translations.literal: Chief ministers entered to offer congratulations; the emperor showed them the picture and documents Xia had submitted and reproached them; all bowed twice and apologized.
