translations.idiomatic: When the chief ministers came to congratulate him, the emperor showed them Xia's picture and memorial and rebuked them; all bowed low in apology.

sentences.zh: 安石上章求去，外間始知所行之由，群奸切齒，遂以俠付御史，治其擅發馬遞罪。

translations.literal: Anshi submitted a memorial asking to leave office; only then did those outside learn the reason for what had been done. The factional villains gnashed their teeth and had Xia handed over to the censorate to punish him for dispatching the courier horse on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi submitted a memorial asking to resign, and only then did the court learn why the measures had been taken. His enemies gnashed their teeth and handed Xia over to the censorate on the charge of dispatching the courier without authorization.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿、鄧綰言於帝曰：「陛下數年以來，忘寐與食，成此美政，天下方被其賜；

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing and Deng Wan said to the emperor, "For several years Your Majesty has forgotten sleep and food to establish this fine governance, and the empire is just receiving its benefits;
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing and Deng Wan told the emperor, "For years Your Majesty has labored without rest to build these excellent policies, and the realm is only now beginning to benefit;

sentences.zh: 一旦用狂夫之言，罷廢殆盡，豈不惜哉？」

translations.literal: yet in a single day, on the word of a madman, nearly all is abolished—is this not to be regretted?"
translations.idiomatic: yet in one day, on the word of a reckless man, nearly all of it is undone—is that not a pity?"

sentences.zh: 相與環泣於帝前，於是新法一切如故。

translations.literal: Together they wept in a circle before the emperor, and thereupon the New Policies all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: They wept together before the throne, and the New Policies were restored in full.

sentences.zh: 安石去，惠卿執政，俠又上疏論之。

translations.literal: When Anshi left, Huiqing took power; Xia again submitted a memorial criticizing this.
translations.idiomatic: After Anshi departed and Huiqing took power, Xia submitted another memorial criticizing the administration.

sentences.zh: 仍取唐魏徵、姚崇、宋璟、李林甫、盧祀傳為兩軸，題曰《正直君子邪曲小人事業圖跡》。

translations.literal: He also took the Tang biographies of Wei Zheng, Yao Chong, Song Jing, Li Linfu, and Lu Qi and made them into two scrolls, entitling them "Pictures and Traces of the Undertakings of Upright Gentlemen and Crooked Petty Men."
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Tang biographies of Wei Zheng, Yao Chong, Song Jing, Li Linfu, and Lu Qi into two scrolls titled "Portraits of the Deeds of Upright Gentlemen and Crooked Petty Men."

sentences.zh: 在位之臣暗合林甫輩而反於崇、璟者，各以其類，復為書獻之。

translations.literal: For ministers in office who secretly matched the Li Linfu sort while turning against Chong and Jing, each according to his kind, he again wrote and presented books.
translations.idiomatic: For ministers in office who secretly resembled Li Linfu and his like while opposing Chong and Jing, he wrote again, grouping each man with his kind, and presented the work to the throne.

sentences.zh: 並言禁中有被甲、登殿等事。

translations.literal: He also spoke of matters such as armored men in the inner palace and ascending the hall.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported rumors of armored men in the inner palace and of armed men entering the hall.

sentences.zh: 惠卿奏為謗訕，編管汀州。

translations.literal: Huiqing memorialized that this was slander and had Xia registered and banished to Tingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing memorialized that this was slander and had Xia placed under registered exile in Tingzhou.

sentences.zh: 御史臺吏楊忠信謁之曰：「御史緘默不言，而君上書不已，是言責在監門而臺中無人也。」

translations.literal: Yang Zhongxin, a clerk of the Censorate, visited him and said, "The censors keep silent while you, sir, keep submitting memorials—this means the duty of speaking lies with the gate supervisor while the censorate has no one."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhongxin, a clerk of the censorate, visited him and said, "The censors remain silent while you keep memorializing—the duty of remonstrance has fallen to a gate supervisor while the censorate stands empty."

sentences.zh: 取懷中《名臣諫疏》二帙授俠曰：「以此為正人助。」

translations.literal: He took from his bosom two volumes of "Memorials of Famous Ministers" and gave them to Xia, saying, "Take these as aid for upright men."
translations.idiomatic: He took two volumes of Memorials of Famous Ministers from his robe and gave them to Xia, saying, "Let these aid the upright."

sentences.zh: 惠卿暴其事，且嗾御史張琥並劾馮京為黨與。

translations.literal: Huiqing exposed the affair and also incited the censor Zhang Hu to impeach Feng Jing as an accomplice.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing made the incident public and also incited Censor Zhang Hu to impeach Feng Jing as Xia's accomplice.

sentences.zh: 俠行至太康，還對獄，獄成，惠卿議致之死。

translations.literal: When Xia reached Taikang he was brought back to face trial; when the case was complete, Huiqing proposed putting him to death.
translations.idiomatic: When Xia reached Taikang he was brought back to stand trial; once the case was closed, Huiqing urged the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「俠所言非為身也，忠誠亦可嘉，豈宜深罪？」

translations.literal: The emperor said, "What Xia spoke was not for himself; his loyalty is also praiseworthy—how can he be deeply punished?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Xia did not speak for his own gain; his loyalty deserves praise—how can he be punished severely?"

sentences.zh: 但徙英州。

translations.literal: He was only exiled to Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was merely exiled to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 既至，得僧屋將壓者居之，英人無貧富貴賤皆加敬，爭遣子弟從學，為築室以遷。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he took up residence in a monk's hall about to collapse; the people of Ying, rich and poor, noble and base, all showed him respect, vied to send their sons to study with him, and built a house for him to move into.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he lived in a monk's hall on the verge of collapse; the people of Ying, high and low alike, honored him, sent their sons to study under him, and built a house for him to move into.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，始得歸。

translations.literal: When Zhezong ascended the throne, he was at last able to return.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhezong came to the throne, he was at last able to return home.

sentences.zh: 蘇軾、孫覺表言之，以為泉州教授。

translations.literal: Su Shi and Sun Jue memorialized on his behalf, and he was appointed professor at Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Su Shi and Sun Jue recommended him in memorials, and he was made professor at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 元符七年，再竄於英。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanfu, he was exiled again to Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanfu 7 he was exiled again to Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 徽宗立，赦之，仍還故官，又為蔡京所奪，自是不復出。

translations.literal: When Huizong ascended the throne, he was amnestied and restored to his former office, but Cai Jing again stripped it from him; from then on he did not leave retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Huizong came to the throne he was pardoned and restored to his former office, but Cai Jing stripped him of it again; from then on he never returned to office.

sentences.zh: 布衣糲食，屏處田野，然一言一話，未嘗忘君。

translations.literal: In plain cloth and coarse food he secluded himself in the countryside, yet in every word and remark he never forgot his ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in plain clothes and coarse fare, secluded in the countryside, yet never forgot his sovereign in word or deed.

sentences.zh: 宣和元年卒，年七十九。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xuanhe, at age seventy-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xuanhe 1, aged seventy-nine.

sentences.zh: 里人揭其閭為「鄭公坊」，州縣皆祀之於學。

translations.literal: Neighbors posted his lane as "Lord Zheng Lane," and prefectures and counties all sacrificed to him in the schools.
translations.idiomatic: Local people named his lane "Lord Zheng Lane," and prefectures and counties all honored him with sacrifices at the schools.

sentences.zh: 紹熙初，詔贈朝奉郎。

translations.literal: Early in Shaoxi, an edict posthumously granted him Court Gentleman for Submission.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shaoxi era, an edict posthumously granted him the rank Court Gentleman for Submission.

sentences.zh: 官其孫嘉正為山陰尉。

translations.literal: His grandson Jiazheng was appointed assistant magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Jiazheng was appointed assistant magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 論曰：誨以言三黜，述、琦、顗窮厄至死，皆充然無悔，身雖不偶，而聲名則昭著於天下後世矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Hui was thrice dismissed for his words; Shu, Qi, and Yi endured hardship to the point of death—all were fully without regret; though their persons did not meet with success, their names are clear and renowned throughout the empire and for generations to come.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Hui was three times dismissed for speaking out; Shu, Qi, and Yi suffered to the point of death—yet none regretted it. Though fortune never favored them, their names shine before the world and posterity.

sentences.zh: 俠以區區小官，雖未信而諫，能以片言悟主，殃民之法幾於一舉而空之，功雖不成，而此心亦足以白於天下後世。

translations.literal: Xia, with his petty minor office, though he remonstrated before he was trusted, was able with a few words to awaken his ruler; the laws that harmed the people were nearly emptied in one stroke; though the achievement was not completed, this heart is also enough to be made clear before the empire and posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Xia held only a minor post, yet though he had not yet earned trust he remonstrated boldly and with a few words moved his ruler; policies that harmed the people were nearly swept away at once. Though success was not complete, his intent stands clear before the world and posterity.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿、鄧綰之罪，可勝誅哉！

translations.literal: The crimes of Lü Huiqing and Deng Wan—can they be punished enough!
translations.idiomatic: The crimes of Lü Huiqing and Deng Wan—no punishment could be enough!
